docs.title: Using enums in Java
docs.text:
The generated enums are nested in their outer Mt4TermApi* class — reference the constant through it:

import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.EnumOpenedOrderSortType;

var op   = OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY;
var sort = EnumOpenedOrderSortType.SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC;

// a value's integer: op.getNumber();  parse a name: OrderSendOperationType.valueOf("OC_OP_BUY")

MT4Service lets you skip the enum entirely for common cases via string mappers (toOperationType("buy","market"), toTimeframe("H1"), toOpenedSort("open_desc")).

docs.title: Special cases
docs.text:
1. Order-operation enums come in three flavours. OrderSendOperationType (OC_OP_*, to send an order), OpenedOrderType (OO_OP_*, the type reported back on open/history orders) and SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (SUB_OP_*, inside streaming events) describe the same six operations but are distinct types — don't mix their value names. OpenedOrderType has two extra non-tradable entries, OO_OP_BALANCE and OO_OP_CREDIT, for balance/credit history records.

2. Return codes are not enums. Trade rejections surface as exceptions carrying an integer MQL code, not a typed enum — see the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every reply from the gateway carries either data or an error; a refused request is a normal answer, not a failed call. JavaMT4 turns that into exceptions so you don't have to inspect every reply by hand — the layers unwrap data for you and throw when the reply holds an error.

All JavaMT4 exceptions are unchecked (extends RuntimeException), so they add no throws noise — but you should still wrap trading calls in try/catch.

docs.title: The exception types
docs.text: Exception Thrown by When ApiExceptionMT4 MT4Account / MT4Service the server answered with an error, or a gRPC call failed ConnectExceptionMT4 MT4Account connect a connection/handshake could not be established MT4Error (+ subclasses) MT4Sugar high-level validation / rejection (see below)

docs.title: ApiExceptionMT4
docs.text:
public MrpcMt4Error.Error getError();   // the server error, or null for a pure transport failure
public String getErrorCode();           // the server error code string, or null
  • Server error: getError() is non-null. Read getErrorCode() (e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND), and for a broker/terminal rejection the MQL fields on the error: getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() (e.g. 131), getError().getMqlErrorDescription(), getError().getMqlErrorCode().
  • Transport failure (network, deadline, server down): getError() is null; getMessage() carries the gRPC status.
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.ApiExceptionMT4;

try {
    account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.001);
} catch (ApiExceptionMT4 e) {
    if (e.getError() != null) {                                    // the server answered with an error
        System.out.println(e.getErrorCode());                      // e.g. MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED
        System.out.println(e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode());     // 131 (invalid trade volume)
        System.out.println(e.getError().getMqlErrorDescription()); // "invalid trade volume"
    } else {
        System.out.println("call failed: " + e.getMessage());      // gRPC status, e.g. UNAVAILABLE
    }
}

docs.title: MT4Error and its subclasses (Sugar layer)
docs.text:
MT4Sugar wraps failures into a small hierarchy (all extend MT4Error, carrying a message, optional code, details and the cause):

Subclass Raised when OrderRejected an entry (placeOrder/buyMarket/…) was refused ModifyRejected a modify/close (modifySlTp…/close/closeBy) was refused RateLimitExceeded the internal order-send rate limiter tripped ConnectivityError a connectivity problem surfaced at the high level

MT4Error itself is also thrown for plain validation (e.g. "not connected", "symbol not found", wait-timeouts).

import pro.mrpc.mt4.error.OrderRejected;

try {
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 100.0, null, null, null, null, null, null, null);  // oversized
} catch (OrderRejected e) {
    System.out.println("entry rejected: " + e.getMessage());   // wraps the underlying ApiExceptionMT4
}

docs.title: Auto-reconnect
docs.text: MT4Account reconnects automatically on a transient UNAVAILABLE or a terminal-not-found error code (TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, TERMINAL_REGISTRY_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND): it sleeps briefly, re-establishes the session and retries the call. Other errors are thrown. So most transient drops never reach your catch.

docs.title: Common MQL rejection codes
docs.text:
When the terminal/broker refuses a trade, getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() carries the MQL code:

Code Meaning What to do 129 invalid price normalize the price to the symbol's digits 130 invalid stops respect TradeStopsLevel (symbol_params_many) 131 invalid trade volume round to VolumeStep, within [VolumeMin, VolumeMax] 132 market closed the session is closed — retry when open 134 not enough money reduce lots / check free margin 145 modify denied order too close to market, or nothing changed

Server-level error codes you'll meet:

errorCode Meaning What to do TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND the terminal id is not a running terminal reconnect (the client does this automatically) MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED the terminal refused the request — see the MQL fields fix the request NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS a tick stream for an unknown/unselected symbol check the symbol / symbolSelect first

docs.title: Getting Started with JavaMT4
docs.text: Quick setup & overview — connect to MetaTrader 4 from Java and make your first calls.

docs.title: What is JavaMT4?
docs.text:
JavaMT4 is the Java SDK for the MRPC MetaTrader 4 gateway (mt4.mrpc.pro:443, gRPC over TLS). It has three layers, each building on the one below:

Layer Class What it gives you 1 — low-level MT4Account raw gRPC calls, auto-reconnect, typed …Data returns 2 — facade MT4Service friendly args (string timeframe/sort, side/type), trade shortcuts 3 — high-level MT4Sugar pip math, risk sizing, trailing/breakeven, watchers

The generated gRPC stubs live under mt4_term_api.* and are compiled with the project; the three layers above wrap them so you rarely touch the stubs directly.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 17+ (the project targets maven.compiler.release = 17).
  • Maven (mvn) or the Maven Daemon (mvnd) — the bundled run.bat auto-detects either.

The project builds the gRPC stubs from package/mt4_term_api/*.java together with the source; there is no separate SDK artifact to install — you run from the cloned repository.

docs.title: Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/JavaMT4.git
cd JavaMT4

Maven coordinates (if you build/install it locally): pro.mrpc:mt4:1.0.0.

docs.title: API key
docs.text:
1. Sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Create a key at https://mrpc.pro/my under API Keys.
  3. Put it in appsettings.json (below). "TRIAL" works for demo accounts.

docs.title: Configure — appsettings.json
docs.text:
The examples read a flat config file at the project root:

{
  "user": 500123456,
  "password": "your_password",
  "serverName": "MetaQuotes-Demo",
  "baseSymbol": "EURUSD",
  "apiKey": "TRIAL"
}
Key Meaning user MT4 account login password account password serverName broker server name (connect-by-name) baseSymbol default symbol the examples trade apiKey MRPC API key ("TRIAL" for demo); MRPC_API_KEY env var overrides it

An optional grpcServer (host:port) overrides the default gateway mt4.mrpc.pro:443.

docs.title: Run an example
docs.text:
run.bat compiles and runs the example launcher (Program), passing the menu number:

run.bat 1          REM low-level market data
run.bat 4          REM MT4Service demo
run.bat 6          REM MT4Sugar basics
run.bat stop       REM stop the Maven daemon

Run run.bat with no argument to see the full menu.

docs.title: Minimal code
docs.text:
Connecting directly through the low-level layer:

import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.AccountSummaryData;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // user, password, grpcServer (null -> mt4.mrpc.pro:443), id (null on first connect), apiKey
        try (MT4Account account = new MT4Account(500123456L, "your_password", null, null, "TRIAL")) {
            account.connectByServerName("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30);

            AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
            System.out.println("Balance: " + s.getAccountBalance() + " " + s.getAccountCurrency());

            var order = account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.01);
            System.out.println("Ticket #" + order.getTicket() + " @ " + order.getPrice());

            account.disconnect(false);   // true also deletes the terminal instance
        }   // close() shuts the gRPC channel down
    }
}

For friendlier arguments wrap it in MT4Service; for one-liners, risk sizing and automation use MT4Sugar.

docs.title: JavaMT4 Glossary
docs.text: Project-specific terms and concepts used throughout the JavaMT4 SDK and these docs.

docs.title: Three-layer architecture
docs.text:
The core design: three decoupled abstraction levels. Your code can enter at any level.

  • Layer 1 — MT4Account: low-level gRPC communication with the MT4 terminal.
  • Layer 2 — MT4Service: typed facade over MT4Account with friendly args and trade shortcuts.
  • Layer 3 — MT4Sugar: high-level one-liners — pip SL/TP, risk sizing, trailing, watchers.

docs.title: MT4Account
docs.text: Base layer: direct gRPC calls to the terminal. Builds the protobuf …Request, retries on transient drops (callWithReconnect), and returns the reply's typed …Data or throws ApiExceptionMT4. 25 feature methods across 5 groups, plus connect/session and streaming helpers. Source: src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java.

docs.title: MT4Service
docs.text: Middle layer wrapping MT4Account one-to-one with friendlier signatures (string timeframe/sort, side/type) and trade shortcuts (buyMarket, sellLimit, close, …) plus setTradeDefaults. Returns the same typed …Data.

docs.title: MT4Sugar
docs.text: High-level layer: pip-based SL/TP, risk-based lot sizing, price/lot normalization, trailing/auto-breakeven workers, batch close/cancel, watchers and waiters. Where most strategies live.

docs.title: Synchronous calls
docs.text: Every request method on MT4Account/MT4Service blocks until the reply arrives and returns the typed payload directly (no Future/callback for ordinary calls). This is the Java counterpart of PyMT4's async/await — you just call the method.

docs.title: Nested value types
docs.text: MT4Sugar returns small plain-data holders instead of protobuf messages: Quote (bid/ask/time), Bar (OHLC + volume), Tick, ExposureBucket, ExposureSummary. They are the Java analogue of PyMT4's dataclasses.

docs.title: Callback streams & Subscription
docs.text: Streaming methods are callback-based: you pass a Consumer<…Data> onData and get back a MT4Account.Subscription (an AutoCloseable). Messages are delivered on a background thread; you stop by closing the subscription. This replaces PyMT4's async generators (async for).

docs.title: try-with-resources / AutoCloseable
docs.text: MT4Account and Subscription implement AutoCloseable, so try (…) { } closes the gRPC channel / cancels the stream automatically — the Java counterpart of Python context managers (async with).

docs.title: Reading account state
docs.text: A one-call snapshot via accountSummary() (balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, server time). Re-query before a risk decision; it's a point-in-time read, not a stream.

docs.title: Normalization
docs.text: Snapping values to broker constraints: lots to the symbol's VolumeStep within [VolumeMin, VolumeMax] (normalizeLot), and prices to the symbol's digit grid (normalizePrice). Sugar does this automatically on entry/modify, preventing ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME (131) / ERR_INVALID_PRICE (129).

docs.title: Risk-based lot calculation
docs.text: calcLotByRisk(symbol, riskPercent, stopPips, balance) turns a risk budget (% of balance over a pip stop) into a normalized lot size, using the symbol's tick value and pip size.

docs.title: Points vs pips
docs.text: A point is the smallest price increment (e.g. 0.00001 on a 5-digit symbol). A pip is the conventional unit — 10 × point on 3/5-digit symbols, else 1 × point. The SDK's SL/TP distances are in pips; the broker's TradeStopsLevel is in points.

docs.title: Pip-based order entry
docs.text: Passing SL/TP as pip distances (slPips/tpPips) rather than absolute prices; Sugar converts them from the entry price via pipSize. Absolute prices (slPrice/tpPrice) are also accepted.

docs.title: Trailing stop
docs.text: A background worker (setTrailingStop) that moves the SL to stay distancePips behind the mid price, only in the favorable direction, optionally throttled by stepPips.

docs.title: Breakeven
docs.text: Moving the SL to the entry price (± a few pips) so the trade can no longer lose. One-shot via closeByBreakeven, or automatic once price runs triggerPips in profit via autoBreakeven.

docs.title: Hedging
docs.text: Holding a BUY and a SELL on the same symbol at once. orderCloseBy / closeBy nets an opposite pair in one operation. Not all brokers permit it.

docs.title: Pending order
docs.text: An order placed away from the market that fills when price reaches it: *LIMIT (toward a better price) or *STOP (on a breakout). Requires an entry price; lives in the same order list until filled or cancelled.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text: The RPC framework the gateway speaks (HTTP/2 + protobuf, TLS). The SDK talks to mt4.mrpc.pro:443; generated stubs live in package/mt4_term_api/.

docs.title: Protobuf
docs.text: The binary message format. Requests/replies are …Request/…Reply messages; each reply carries either data (a typed …Data) or an error. The SDK unwraps data for you.

docs.title: Return codes & errors
docs.text: MT4 has no numeric returned_code; failures are exceptions (ApiExceptionMT4, or MT4Error subclasses at the Sugar layer). The MQL4 code lives in getError().getMqlErrorIntCode(). See the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: Streaming pattern
docs.text: Server-push over gRPC streams, surfaced as callback Subscriptions with built-in auto-reconnect. See Streams.

docs.title: Basic terms
docs.text:
• Bid / Ask — sell price / buy price; spread = ask − bid.
  • Lot — trade volume unit (1.0 = standard; 0.01 = micro).
  • SL / TP — stop-loss / take-profit exit prices.
  • Ticket — the order's unique id.
  • Magic number — a tag you attach to identify "your" orders.
  • Balance vs Equity — balance excludes open P/L; equity = balance + floating P/L.
  • Margin / Free margin / Margin level — collateral used / available / equity÷margin %.

docs.title: Risk amount
docs.text: The cash you're willing to lose on a trade (e.g. 1% of balance). calcCashRisk(symbol, lots, stopPips) values a stop in cash; calcLotByRisk inverts it to a lot size.

docs.title: Grid trading
docs.text: Placing layered pending orders at fixed intervals around price. Build it from buyLimit/sellStop entries and manage with cancelPendings / closeAll.

docs.title: Scalping
docs.text: Many short-lived trades for small per-trade gains; sensitive to spread (spreadPips) and latency.

docs.title: News trading (OCO straddle)
docs.text: Placing a buy-stop above and a sell-stop below price before a news release to catch the breakout; cancel the un-triggered side afterward (cancelPendings).

docs.title: Volume limits
docs.text: Per-symbol VolumeMin / VolumeMax / VolumeStep (and sometimes VolumeLimit) from symbolParamsMany; normalizeLot enforces them.

docs.title: Settings file — appsettings.json
docs.text: The flat config the examples read: user, password, serverName, baseSymbol, apiKey (+ optional grpcServer). MRPC_API_KEY overrides the key. See Getting Started.

docs.title: Batch operations
docs.text: Acting on many orders at once: closeAll(symbol, magic, onlyProfit), cancelPendings(symbol, magic) — filtered bulk exits that loop the open list for you.

docs.title: History queries
docs.text: Reading closed orders over a window with sort/paging: ordersHistory(sort, since, until, page, pageSize); aggregate stats via tradeStats / tradeStatsEquityHistory.

docs.title: Educational project
docs.text: The bundled examples/ and strategies/ are learning material — demo-account oriented, 0.01-lot, self-cleaning. Not production trading advice.

docs.title: Exception handling
docs.text: All SDK exceptions are unchecked (extends RuntimeException): ApiExceptionMT4, ConnectExceptionMT4, and the MT4Error family (OrderRejected, ModifyRejected, RateLimitExceeded, ConnectivityError). Wrap trading calls in try/catch; see Errors.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text: Generated enums are nested in their outer Mt4TermApi* class — e.g. Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY. The three operation-enum flavours (OC_OP_*, OO_OP_*, SUB_OP_*) are distinct types; see the ENUMs Usage Reference.

docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT4Sugar. Pip-based SL/TP, risk sizing and auto-normalization protect you from off-quote and invalid-volume rejections.

docs.title: 🛡️ How MT4 reports errors
docs.text:
Unlike MT5 (which returns a numeric returned_code / TRADE_RETCODE_* on every trade result), MT4 reports failures as exceptions. A trading call either:

  • succeeds — and returns its data (e.g. orderSend returns a ticket), or
  • fails — and throws an exception carrying a structured error.

There is no returned_code field and no TRADE_RETCODE_* constants in JavaMT4. The classic MQL4 error codes live in the MqlErrorCode enum (below).

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
import pro.mrpc.mt4.ApiExceptionMT4;

try {
    long ticket = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01, null, null, null, null, null, null, null);
    System.out.println("✓ opened #" + ticket);
} catch (ApiExceptionMT4 e) {
    var err = e.getError();   // the structured protobuf Error (null for a transport failure)
    if (err != null)
        System.out.printf("✗ trade failed: %s (code %d)%n", err.getMqlErrorDescription(), err.getMqlErrorIntCode());
}

Key point: no exception = the trade went through; an exception tells you why it did not.

docs.title: Where the codes come from
docs.text: The codes are the standard MQL4 error codes, defined in the protobuf enum MqlErrorCode inside package/mt4_term_api/MrpcMt4Error.java. They are returned by the trading server and mirror what GetLastError() returns inside an MQL4 EA.

docs.title: How errors surface in the API
Low level — MT4Account
docs.text:
Exception When ConnectExceptionMT4 a method was called before a connect, or a connection could not be established ApiExceptionMT4 the server returned an error for the request (or a gRPC call failed)

ApiExceptionMT4.getError() returns a protobuf Error with these getters:

Field Getter Meaning type getType() high-level category (ErrorType): MRPC, MRPC_VALIDATION, MRPC_TIMEOUT, MQL_EXECUTION, … error_code getErrorCode() gateway error code string (e.g. MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED) error_message getErrorMessage() human-readable gateway message mql_error_code getMqlErrorCode() symbolic MQL4 error (e.g. ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY) mql_error_int_code getMqlErrorIntCode() numeric MQL4 error (e.g. 134) mql_error_description getMqlErrorDescription() description of the MQL4 error command_type_name getCommandTypeName() which RPC produced the error

ApiExceptionMT4.getErrorCode() is a shortcut to the server error-code string (or null).

docs.title: High level — MT4Sugar
docs.text:
The Sugar layer wraps failures into domain exceptions (all extend MT4Error):

Exception Raised for OrderRejected placeOrder / buyMarket / … failures ModifyRejected modifySlTp… / close / closeBy failures ConnectivityError reconnect / session / handshake issues RateLimitExceeded the client-side rate-limit guard tripped MT4Error base class / plain validation (not connected, symbol not found, wait timeout)

Each MT4Error carries the message (wrapping the low-level error), plus optional code/details and the cause.

docs.title: Low level (MT4Account)
docs.text:
import pro.mrpc.mt4.ApiExceptionMT4;

try {
    var result = account.orderSend(request);
    System.out.printf("✓ order #%d @ %.5f%n", result.getTicket(), result.getPrice());
} catch (ApiExceptionMT4 e) {
    int code = e.getError() != null ? e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() : -1;
    switch (code) {
        case 134 -> System.out.println("Not enough money — reduce volume or add margin");
        case 132 -> System.out.println("Market is closed — try during trading hours");
        default  -> System.out.println("Trade failed: " + e.getMessage() + " (code " + code + ")");
    }
}

import pro.mrpc.mt4.error.OrderRejected;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.error.MT4Error;

try {

} catch (OrderRejected e) {

} catch (MT4Error e) {

}

docs.title: Retrying transient errors
docs.text:
Some codes are temporary and safe to retry with a short backoff: ERR_SERVER_BUSY (4), ERR_NO_CONNECTION (6), ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS (8), ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT (128), ERR_PRICE_CHANGED (135), ERR_OFF_QUOTES (136), ERR_BROKER_BUSY (137), ERR_REQUOTE (138), ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY (146), ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS (141).

static final Set<Integer> RETRYABLE = Set.of(4, 6, 8, 128, 135, 136, 137, 138, 141, 146);

static long buyWithRetry(MT4Sugar sugar, String symbol, double lots, int maxRetries) throws InterruptedException {
    for (int attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
        try {
            return sugar.buyMarket(symbol, lots, null, null, null, null, null, null, null);
        } catch (pro.mrpc.mt4.ApiExceptionMT4 e) {
            int code = e.getError() != null ? e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() : -1;
            if (RETRYABLE.contains(code) && attempt < maxRetries) {
                Thread.sleep(attempt * 1000L);   // 1s, 2s, …
                continue;
            }
            throw e;
        }
    }
}

Permanent errors (don't retry): ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY (134), ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130), ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME (131), ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132), ERR_TRADE_DISABLED (133). Fix the request or conditions.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
✅ DO

  1. Wrap trading calls in try/catch — that's how MT4 reports failures.
  2. Branch on e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() for the exact reason.
  3. Retry only transient codes with a short backoff.

❌ DON'T

  1. Don't look for a returned_code — MT4 has none; a returned ticket already means success.
  2. Don't retry permanent errors (insufficient money, invalid stops, market closed).
  3. Don't swallow exceptions silently — log getMqlErrorDescription().

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Category Codes Action Success 0 + a returned ticket continue Transient 4, 6, 8, 128, 135, 136, 137, 138, 141, 146 retry with delay Invalid request 3, 129, 130, 131 fix parameters Restrictions 132, 133, 140, 149, 150 check trading conditions Limits 134, 148 reduce volume / close orders Account / rights 7, 64, 65 check account & permissions

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
The gateway pushes real-time data over gRPC server streams. In JavaMT4 every stream is a callback subscription: you pass a Consumer<…Data> onData (and an optional Consumer<Throwable> onError), and the call returns a MT4Account.Subscription — an AutoCloseable you close to stop.

Method (MT4Account / MT4Service) What it delivers onSymbolTick bid/ask ticks for the given symbols onTrade trade events — new / updated / removed orders onOpenedOrdersProfit floating P/L of open orders, on a timer onOpenedOrdersTickets open position & pending ticket lists, sampled onConnectState terminal connection-state changes

docs.title: Using a stream
docs.text:
Close the subscription to stop it — try-with-resources is the clean way:

import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;

// account: a connected MT4Account
try (MT4Account.Subscription s = account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(1000, ev -> {
        double total = ev.getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList().stream()
                .mapToDouble(o -> o.getOrderProfit()).sum();
        System.out.printf("floating P/L: %+.2f%n", total);
    }, err -> System.err.println("stream error: " + err.getMessage()))) {

    TimeUnit.SECONDS.sleep(10);   // consume for 10 s
}   // close() cancels the stream

If you don't use try-with-resources, keep the returned Subscription and call close() when done.

docs.title: How subscriptions behave
docs.text:
• One callback per message. onData is invoked on a background thread for each update; keep per-message work light (offload heavy processing to a queue/executor).
  • Auto-reconnect is built in. A transient gRPC drop reopens the stream under the hood and keeps delivering to your callback — you don't re-subscribe.
  • onError is invoked for a terminal stream error; it may be null (errors are then swallowed after reconnect attempts).
  • Close to stop. Nothing stops a stream except closing its Subscription (or closing the owning MT4Account). An unclosed subscription keeps its reconnect loop alive.
  • Quiet markets deliver nothing. Tick/trade streams are silent on a closed market; the ticket/profit/connect-state streams are timer- or state-driven and still fire.

docs.title: Through the higher layers
docs.text:
• MT4Service exposes the same five methods with the same Consumer/Subscription shape.
  • MT4Sugar wraps them as watchers (watchTicks, watchProfit, …) that return a String id and are stopped with unwatch(id) — handy when you want the SDK to track the subscription for you.

docs.title: Step 4 — Write your own
docs.text:
Create a small main that connects, reads the account, buys 0.01 lot of EURUSD and closes it. This uses the high-level MT4Sugar layer so SL/TP are in pips and lots/prices are normalized for you:

import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Service;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Sugar;

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        try (MT4Account account = new MT4Account(500123456L, "your_password", null, null, "TRIAL")) {
            account.connectByServerName("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30);

            MT4Sugar sugar = new MT4Sugar(new MT4Service(account));

            var acc = account.accountSummary();
            System.out.printf("Balance: %.2f %s%n", acc.getAccountBalance(), acc.getAccountCurrency());

            long ticket = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01, 50.0, 100.0, null, null, "first", null, null);
            System.out.println("opened #" + ticket);
            sugar.waitFilled((int) ticket, 10_000L);

            Thread.sleep(1000);
            sugar.close((int) ticket);
            System.out.println("closed #" + ticket);

            account.disconnect(false);
        }
    }
}

⚠️ This places a real order on the connected (demo) account — keep it to 0.01 lots and always close what you open.

docs.title: MT4Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: the low-level gRPC client for MetaTrader 4. Jump to any group overview or method spec from here.

MT4Account is Layer 1 — direct gRPC/protobuf calls to the MT4 terminal gateway. MT4Service (typed facade) and MT4Sugar (high-level helpers) build on top of it.

It exposes 25 feature methods across 5 groups (plus connection & stream helpers). MT4 has a single order list — no positions/deals split, Depth-of-Market, order_check or order_calc_* (those are MT5-only).

Defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java.

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (Java)
docs.text:
MT4Account is synchronous and implements AutoCloseable: each call blocks until the reply arrives, returns the reply's typed …Data payload, or throws ApiExceptionMT4 on a server-side error. Wrap it in try-with-resources so the gRPC channel is always closed.

import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.AccountSummaryData;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType;

try (MT4Account account = new MT4Account(12345678L, "your_password", null, null, "TRIAL")) {
    // null grpcServer -> defaults to mt4.mrpc.pro:443 (TLS)
    account.connectByServerName("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30);

    AccountSummaryData summary = account.accountSummary();
    System.out.println(summary.getAccountBalance() + " " + summary.getAccountEquity());

    account.orderSend("EURUSD", OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, 0.01);

    account.disconnect(false);
}   // close() shuts the channel down

docs.title: 🧱 How the call contract works
docs.text:
Every feature method follows the same shape:

  1. ensureConnected() — fail fast if connect… has not run.
  2. Build the protobuf …Request.
  3. callWithReconnect(...) — invoke the gRPC stub; on UNAVAILABLE or a terminal-not-found error code it reconnects and retries automatically; any other error is thrown.
  4. dataOf(reply) — unwrap the reply's data field, or throw ApiExceptionMT4 carrying the reply's error.

So you always get the typed …Data object directly — never a raw …Reply with a nested error to check by hand.

Arg Meaning user MT4 account login password account password grpcServer gateway host:port; null → mt4.mrpc.pro:443 id terminal instance id; null on first connect (the gateway assigns one) apiKey API key; "TRIAL" works for demo

Connect with either the broker's server name or an explicit host/port:

account.connectByHostPort("mt4live.broker.com", 443, 30);      // by address

docs.title: 1. Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
The account's money picture and its performance history: a one-call snapshot, aggregate trade statistics, the equity curve, and unrealized-P/L extrema.

These five methods are read-only — they never touch orders. They are the first calls most bots make: a snapshot at startup, then statistics/equity for dashboards and risk checks.

All of them live on the mt4_term_api.AccountHelper and mt4_term_api.TradeStats gRPC services and return a typed …Data payload.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner accountSummary() AccountSummaryData Balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, server time — one round-trip. tradeStats(from) StatsData Aggregate performance: win rate, profit factor, drawdowns, Sharpe, expectancy… tradeUnrealizedPl(from) TradeUnrealizedPLData Per-order max/min floating-P/L extrema (MFE / MAE). equityHistory(from, excludeSameBars) EquityHistoryData The equity/balance curve as time-stamped points. tradeStatsEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars) StatsWithChartsData Stats + equity chart + closed trades, all in one call.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• Just connected / banner / sanity check → accountSummary().
  • Pre-trade risk gate (free margin, margin level, trading allowed) → accountSummary().
  • Performance dashboard (win rate, profit factor, drawdown) → tradeStats(), or tradeStatsEquityHistory() when you also want the curve and the trade list.
  • Equity/drawdown chart → equityHistory().
  • Trade-quality analysis (how far each trade ran in your favour/against you) → tradeUnrealizedPl().

docs.title: Shared argument — from
docs.text:
tradeStats, tradeUnrealizedPl, equityHistory and tradeStatsEquityHistory all take an optional from of type java.time.Instant:

  • null → the server's default window (usually the whole account history).
  • a value → only data at or after that instant.

In Java it is sent to the server as an ISO-8601 string (from.toString()), so pass a UTC Instant (e.g. Instant.now().minus(30, ChronoUnit.DAYS)).

docs.title: Account Summary (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Complete account snapshot (balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, server time) in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.accountSummary() (defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) -> AccountSummaryReply
  • Payload: AccountSummaryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One call that returns every essential account property.
  • Why you need it. The most efficient way to read balance/equity/margin at once — one round-trip instead of many single-field calls.
  • When to use. At session start (banner / sanity check), and right before any risk decision or order.

docs.text:
• RECOMMENDED way to read account state
  • Balance, equity, credit in one round-trip
  • Login, name, server, company
  • Leverage and trade mode (DEMO/REAL)
  • Currency and server time

public AccountSummaryData accountSummary()

No arguments. Returns the typed payload directly, or throws ApiExceptionMT4 on a server error.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call beats many. accountSummary() returns balance, equity, margin, free margin and margin level together — don't fan out into several calls for these.
  • balance vs equity. Balance ignores open orders; equity includes their floating P/L. On a flat account they're equal; with open orders, equity − balance is your current floating P/L.
  • Money is in the deposit currency. Every monetary field is in account_currency. Don't mix it with an instrument's quote currency without converting.
  • margin_level is 0 with no open orders (division by zero margin is reported as 0), so guard before comparing it to a stop-out threshold.
  • Server time. server_time / server_time_utc are protobuf Timestamps — convert with Instant.ofEpochSecond(ts.getSeconds(), ts.getNanos()); server_utc_offset_seconds tells you the broker's offset.
  • Read-only sessions. If is_investor is true (investor password) or account_trade_allowed is false, trading calls will be rejected — check these before placing orders.

docs.title: 1) Session-start banner
docs.text:
Print a clean account banner when your bot connects — handy for logs and sanity checks.

import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.AccountSummaryData;
import mt4_term_api.Mt4TermApiAccountHelper.EnumAccountTradeMode;
import java.util.Locale;

static void printBanner(MT4Account account) {
    AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
    double floating = s.getAccountEquity() - s.getAccountBalance();
    String mode = switch (s.getAccountTradeMode()) {
        case ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO -> "DEMO";
        case ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST -> "CONTEST";
        case ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL -> "REAL";
        default -> "?";
    };
    System.out.println("=".repeat(52));
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Account #%d  (%s)%n", s.getAccountLogin(), mode);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Broker : %s%n", s.getAccountCompanyName());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Balance: %,.2f %s%n", s.getAccountBalance(), s.getAccountCurrency());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Equity : %,.2f  (floating %+,.2f)%n", s.getAccountEquity(), floating);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Margin : used %,.2f / free %,.2f%n", s.getAccountMargin(), s.getAccountMarginFree());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Leverage 1:%d%n", s.getAccountLeverage());
    System.out.println("=".repeat(52));
}

docs.title: 2) Pre-trade risk gate
docs.text:
Refuse to open a new order unless the account can actually take it — a guard you call before every entry.

static boolean canOpen(MT4Account account, double minFreeMargin, double minMarginLevel) {
    AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();

    if (!s.getAccountTradeAllowed() || s.getIsInvestor()) {
        System.out.println("Trading not allowed on this account (read-only / disabled).");
        return false;
    }
    if (s.getAccountMarginFree() < minFreeMargin) {
        System.out.printf("Free margin too low: %.2f < %.2f%n", s.getAccountMarginFree(), minFreeMargin);
        return false;
    }
    // margin_level is 0 when nothing is open — only enforce it once there is margin in use
    if (s.getAccountMargin() > 0 && s.getAccountMarginLevel() < minMarginLevel) {
        System.out.printf("Margin level too low: %.1f%% < %.1f%%%n", s.getAccountMarginLevel(), minMarginLevel);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// usage:
// if (canOpen(account, 500, 200.0)) sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.10, ...);

docs.title: 3) Equity / drawdown monitor
docs.text:
Poll equity on an interval and alert when drawdown from the session peak crosses a limit.

static void watchDrawdown(MT4Account account, double maxDdPercent, long intervalMs) throws InterruptedException {
    Double peak = null;
    while (true) {
        double eq = account.accountSummary().getAccountEquity();
        peak = (peak == null) ? eq : Math.max(peak, eq);
        double dd = peak > 0 ? (peak - eq) / peak * 100 : 0.0;
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "equity=%,.2f peak=%,.2f drawdown=%.2f%%%n", eq, peak, dd);
        if (dd >= maxDdPercent) {
            System.out.printf("[ALERT] drawdown %.2f%% >= %.1f%% — consider de-risking%n", dd, maxDdPercent);
            break;
        }
        Thread.sleep(intervalMs);
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not a stream. Equity/margin are a point-in-time read — re-query right before a risk check or order, don't cache them across time. (For live updates use onOpenedOrdersProfit.)
  • margin_level == 0 with nothing open. Guard account_margin > 0 before comparing the level to a stop-out/entry threshold.
  • Currency mismatch. All money fields are in account_currency; converting instrument P/L into account currency is on you.
  • Read-only / disabled accounts. is_investor or account_trade_allowed == false means orders will be rejected even though this call succeeds.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo). Fields are populated; account_currency non-empty; on a flat account equity == balance and account_margin == 0.
  • With open orders. equity != balance, account_margin > 0, and account_margin_level is a sensible percentage.
  • Risk gate. Unit-test canOpen() against synthetic summaries (low free margin, investor session, trading disabled) and assert it refuses.

docs.title: Equity Curve
docs.text:
Time series of balance/equity points with running drawdowns — your equity curve, ready to chart or export.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.equityHistory(Instant from, Boolean excludeSameBars) (defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: EquityHistory(EquityHistoryRequest) -> EquityHistoryReply
  • Payload: EquityHistoryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A chronological list of points, each with balance, equity, running drawdowns and the cash flow at that moment.
  • Why you need it. To plot the equity curve, measure maximum drawdown, or export performance to a spreadsheet.
  • When to use. Reporting, charting, drawdown analysis.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Balance & equity over time (the curve)
  • Running balance/equity drawdowns (money and %)
  • Realized / unrealized P/L and cash flow per point
  • Feed charts, CSV exports and risk reports

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public EquityHistoryData equityHistory(Instant from, Boolean excludeSameBars)

from is an optional UTC Instant (pass null for full history); excludeSameBars is a Boolean (pass null to leave it unset).

Request message:

message EquityHistoryRequest {
  string from = 1;              // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  bool exclude_same_bars = 2;   // collapse consecutive equal points
  string from_utc = 3;          // ISO-8601 start in UTC
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message EquityHistoryData {
  repeated EquityPointData points = 1;
}

message EquityPointData {
  Timestamp time = 1;
  double balance = 2;
  double equity = 3;
  double balance_drawdown_raw = 4;
  double balance_drawdown_relative = 5;    // percent
  double equity_drawdown_raw = 6;
  double equity_drawdown_relative = 7;     // percent
  double realized_pl = 8;
  double unrealized_pl = 9;
  Timestamp time_utc = 10;
  double cash_flow = 11;                    // deposits/withdrawals at this point
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from Instant, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Pass null for full history. excludeSameBars Boolean, optional Collapse consecutive equal points to shrink the payload. Pass null to leave unset.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — EquityHistoryData
docs.text:
Field Java getter Description points getPointsCount() / getPoints(i) / getPointsList() The equity-curve points, in time order

Each EquityPointData:

Field Java getter Description time / time_utc getTime() / getTimeUtc() Point timestamp (server / UTC) balance getBalance() Balance at this point equity getEquity() Equity at this point balance_drawdown_raw / _relative getBalanceDrawdownRaw() / getBalanceDrawdownRelative() Balance drawdown (money / %) equity_drawdown_raw / _relative getEquityDrawdownRaw() / getEquityDrawdownRelative() Equity drawdown (money / %) realized_pl getRealizedPl() Realized P/L to this point unrealized_pl getUnrealizedPl() Floating P/L at this point cash_flow getCashFlow() Deposit/withdrawal applied at this point

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Drawdowns are precomputed. You don't have to derive the running peak yourself — getEquityDrawdownRelative() is already the % below the high-water mark at each point.
  • cash_flow separates deposits from trading. A jump in balance with a matching cash_flow is a deposit/withdrawal, not a trade — exclude it when measuring trading performance.
  • This payload can be large. A long-lived account has many points; pass from to scope the window and/or excludeSameBars = true to drop flat stretches.
  • Timestamps are protobuf Timestamps — convert with Instant.ofEpochSecond(ts.getSeconds(), ts.getNanos()).
  • Pairs with trade_stats. Use tradeStats for the headline ratios and equityHistory for the curve, or tradeStatsEquityHistory to fetch both at once.

docs.title: 1) Export the curve to CSV
docs.text:
Dump the equity curve so you can chart it in a spreadsheet or notebook.

static void exportEquityCsv(MT4Account account, Path path) throws IOException {
    var data = account.equityHistory(null, true);
    try (var w = Files.newBufferedWriter(path)) {
        w.write("time_utc,balance,equity,equity_dd_%\n");
        for (var p : data.getPointsList()) {
            var t = Instant.ofEpochSecond(p.getTimeUtc().getSeconds());
            w.write(String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%s,%.2f,%.2f,%.2f%n",
                    t, p.getBalance(), p.getEquity(), p.getEquityDrawdownRelative()));
        }
    }
    System.out.printf("wrote %d points -> %s%n", data.getPointsCount(), path);
}

docs.title: 2) Maximum drawdown from the curve
docs.text:
Find the deepest equity drawdown and when it happened.

static void maxDrawdown(MT4Account account) {
    var data = account.equityHistory(null, null);
    if (data.getPointsCount() == 0) { System.out.println("no equity history"); return; }
    var worst = data.getPointsList().stream()
            .max(Comparator.comparingDouble(p -> p.getEquityDrawdownRelative())).orElseThrow();
    var when = Instant.ofEpochSecond(worst.getTimeUtc().getSeconds());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "Max equity drawdown: %.2f%% (%,.2f) at %s UTC%n",
            worst.getEquityDrawdownRelative(), worst.getEquityDrawdownRaw(), when);
}

docs.title: 3) Trading-only result (strip deposits)
docs.text:
Separate trading performance from deposits/withdrawals using cash_flow.

static double tradingPnl(MT4Account account) {
    var pts = account.equityHistory(null, null).getPointsList();
    if (pts.isEmpty()) return 0.0;
    double netCash = pts.stream().mapToDouble(p -> p.getCashFlow()).sum();
    double start = pts.get(0).getBalance(), end = pts.get(pts.size() - 1).getBalance();
    double trading = (end - start) - netCash;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "balance %,.2f -> %,.2f | deposits/withdrawals %+,.2f | trading P/L %+,.2f%n",
            start, end, netCash, trading);
    return trading;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Large payloads. Full history can be big — scope with from and/or excludeSameBars = true; print counts rather than every point.
  • Deposits skew raw balance deltas. Use cash_flow to isolate trading P/L from account funding.
  • Empty history. A fresh account returns an empty points list — guard before indexing getPoints(0) / the last element.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). points is non-empty and ordered by time; equity_drawdown_relative >= 0 for every point.
  • excludeSameBars. The collapsed call returns no more points than the full call.
  • Windowing. A recent from returns fewer points than full history.

docs.title: Trade Statistics
docs.text:
Aggregated trade statistics — profit factor, win/loss, drawdowns, expectancy and a per-market breakdown, in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tradeStats(Instant from) (defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: TradeStats(TradeStatsRequest) -> TradeStatsReply
  • Payload: StatsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A rollup of your trading performance: headline ratios, drawdowns, and a breakdown per market.
  • Why you need it. The numbers a dashboard or weekly review needs — without computing them yourself from raw history.
  • When to use. Reporting, periodic performance checks, "how am I doing?" screens.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Profit factor, expectancy, Sharpe ratio, GHPR, Z-score
  • Win/loss counts and percentages
  • Balance & equity drawdowns (absolute and relative)
  • Per-market breakdown (trades, lots, profit, win rate)
  • Account totals: deposits, withdrawals, growth %

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• summary is the "today/this week/this month" block — perfect for a compact P/L widget, separate from the all-time ratios.
  • Drawdowns come in two flavours: balance vs equity, each as raw money and relative %. Equity drawdown is usually the one that matters for risk.
  • markets is your per-symbol attribution — iterate getMarketsCount() / getMarkets(i) to see which instruments actually make or lose money.
  • Watch the proto spelling. Field names carry the server's spelling: comissions, tiket, won_persent → getters are getComissions(), getTiket(), getWonPersent() — use them as-is.
  • from trims the window. Pass null for the full account history; pass an Instant to scope stats to a period (e.g. this month).
  • Pairs with equity_history. Use tradeStats for the numbers and equityHistory for the curve, or tradeStatsEquityHistory to get both in one round-trip.

docs.title: 1) Weekly performance report
docs.text:
Turn the stats into a readable report line — the kind you log or post to a channel.

static void performanceReport(MT4Account account) {
    var s = account.tradeStats(null);
    var p = s.getProfitability();
    System.out.println("── Performance ──────────────────────────────");
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Trades        : %d  (win %.1f%%)%n", s.getTrades(), p.getWonTradesPercent());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Profit factor : %.2f%n", s.getProfitFactor());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Expectancy    : %+.2f / trade%n", s.getExpectancy().getDollar());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Growth        : %+.2f%%%n", s.getGrowthPercent());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Max DD (eq)   : %.1f%%  (%,.2f)%n",
            s.getMaxEquityDrawdownRelative(), s.getMaxEquityDrawdownRaw());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " This week     : %+,.2f%n", s.getSummary().getWeekProfit());
}

docs.title: 2) Which markets make money?
docs.text:
Rank the per-market breakdown so you can cut the losers and size up the winners.

static void marketsByProfit(MT4Account account, int top) {
    var s = account.tradeStats(null);
    var rows = new ArrayList<>(s.getMarketsList());
    rows.sort(Comparator.comparingDouble(MarketTradeCountData::getProfit).reversed());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-10s%7s%7s%12s%n", "Symbol", "Trades", "Win%", "Profit");
    for (var m : rows.subList(0, Math.min(top, rows.size()))) {
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-10s%7d%6.1f%%%12,.2f%n",
                m.getMarketName(), m.getCount(), m.getWinRate(), m.getProfit());
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Month-to-date health check
docs.text:
Scope the stats to the current month and flag a weak profit factor.

static boolean monthHealth(MT4Account account, double minProfitFactor) {
    Instant start = YearMonth.now(ZoneOffset.UTC).atDay(1).atStartOfDay(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant();
    var s = account.tradeStats(start);
    boolean ok = s.getProfitFactor() >= minProfitFactor;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "MTD: trades=%d PF=%.2f result=%+,.2f -> %s%n",
            s.getTrades(), s.getProfitFactor(), s.getSummary().getMonthProfit(), ok ? "OK" : "WEAK");
    return ok;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty history. A brand-new account with no closed trades returns zeroed stats — guard divisions (e.g. don't trust profit_factor when trades == 0).
  • Potentially heavy. The markets list grows with the number of traded symbols; summarize rather than print everything.
  • Spelling quirks. getComissions(), getTiket(), getWonPersent() are the real getter names — a typo-looking call is correct.
  • Scope awareness. Numbers reflect the from window (or all history if null) — don't compare a month-scoped call with an all-time one.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). getTrades() > 0, getProfitFactor() finite, getMarketsCount() >= 1.
  • Fresh account. With no closed trades, assert the call still succeeds and your report handles zeros without dividing by zero.
  • Windowing. A from of today vs a year ago returns different trades counts; assert the scoped count ≤ the full count.

docs.title: Stats + Equity + Trades
docs.text:
Statistics, the equity curve and the trade list — everything a performance report needs, in a single round-trip.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tradeStatsEquityHistory(Instant from, Boolean excludeSameBars) (defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: TradeStatsEquityHistory(TradeStatsEquityHistoryRequest) -> TradeStatsEquityHistoryReply
  • Payload: StatsWithChartsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A combined payload: the same StatsData as trade_stats, the equity charts (same points as equity_history), plus the closed and open trade lists.
  • Why you need it. Build a full report (numbers + curve + trades) without three separate calls.
  • When to use. Report/export screens where you want everything consistent and in one shot.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Headline statistics (stats)
  • Equity-curve points (charts)
  • Closed trades (trades) and currently open trades (open_trades)
  • One round-trip for a complete report

docs.text:
public StatsWithChartsData tradeStatsEquityHistory(Instant from, Boolean excludeSameBars)

from is an optional UTC Instant (pass null for full history); excludeSameBars is a Boolean (pass null to leave it unset).

Request message:

message TradeStatsEquityHistoryRequest {
  string from = 1;              // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  bool exclude_same_bars = 2;   // collapse consecutive equal equity points
  string from_utc = 3;          // ISO-8601 start in UTC
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message StatsWithChartsData {
  StatsData stats = 1;                         // see trade_stats
  repeated EquityPointData charts = 2;         // see equity_history
  repeated TradeHistoryItemData trades = 3;    // closed trades
  repeated TradeHistoryItemData open_trades = 4;
}

message TradeHistoryItemData {
  int64 ticket = 1;
  string symbol = 2;
  bool is_buy = 3;
  double lots = 4;
  double open_price = 5;
  double close_price = 6;
  Timestamp open_time = 7;
  Timestamp close_time = 8;
  double profit = 9;
  double commission = 10;
  double swap = 11;
  string comment = 12;
  Timestamp open_time_utc = 13;
  Timestamp close_time_utc = 14;
}

docs.text: Parameter Type Description from Instant, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Pass null for full history. excludeSameBars Boolean, optional Collapse consecutive equal equity points to shrink charts. Pass null to leave unset.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call, three views. stats is the summary, charts is the curve, trades/open_trades are the raw rows — everything stays consistent because it's a single snapshot.
  • Net result per trade is getProfit() + getCommission() + getSwap() (commission and swap are usually negative). Don't forget the costs when totalling.
  • is_buy is the side — there's no separate order-type enum here; true = long, false = short.
  • Can be large. charts and trades grow with account age — scope with from and excludeSameBars = true for the curve.
  • Prefer this over three calls when you need all three together; use the individual methods when you only need one.

docs.title: 1) Full report in one round-trip
docs.text:
Pull everything and print a compact report header.

static void fullReport(MT4Account account) {
    var r = account.tradeStatsEquityHistory(null, true);
    var s = r.getStats();
    System.out.println("── Report ───────────────────────────────────");
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Profit factor : %.2f%n", s.getProfitFactor());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Trades        : %d  (open now: %d)%n", s.getTrades(), r.getOpenTradesCount());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Growth        : %+.2f%%%n", s.getGrowthPercent());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Equity points : %d%n", r.getChartsCount());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, " Closed trades : %d%n", r.getTradesCount());
}

docs.title: 2) Recent closed trades table
docs.text:
Show the last few closed trades with side, size and net result.

static void recentTrades(MT4Account account, int n) {
    var rows = new ArrayList<>(account.tradeStatsEquityHistory(null, null).getTradesList());
    rows.sort(Comparator.comparingLong((TradeHistoryItemData t) -> t.getCloseTimeUtc().getSeconds()).reversed());
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10s %-8s %-5s %6s %10s%n", "Ticket", "Sym", "Side", "Lots", "Net");
    for (var t : rows.subList(0, Math.min(n, rows.size()))) {
        double net = t.getProfit() + t.getCommission() + t.getSwap();
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10d %-8s %-5s %6.2f %10.2f%n",
                t.getTicket(), t.getSymbol(), t.getIsBuy() ? "BUY" : "SELL", t.getLots(), net);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Open exposure right now
docs.text:
Summarize current open trades (count, lots, floating P/L) straight from open_trades.

static void openExposure(MT4Account account) {
    var open = account.tradeStatsEquityHistory(null, null).getOpenTradesList();
    double lots = open.stream().mapToDouble(t -> t.getLots()).sum();
    double floating = open.stream().mapToDouble(t -> t.getProfit() + t.getCommission() + t.getSwap()).sum();
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "open trades: %d | lots: %.2f | floating: %+.2f%n", open.size(), lots, floating);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Heaviest call in the group. It returns stats + curve + every trade — scope it (from, excludeSameBars) and summarize rather than dumping all rows.
  • Costs are separate. profit excludes commission and swap; add them for the true net.
  • Empty account. trades, open_trades and charts can all be empty — guard before indexing.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). stats.getTrades() equals getTradesCount() for the same window; charts is non-empty.
  • Open vs closed. getOpenTradesCount() matches what opened_orders reports.
  • Consistency. stats here equals a separate trade_stats call over the same from.

docs.text:
For each open order, the best and worst floating P/L it has reached (with timestamps) — classic MFE / MAE excursion data.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tradeUnrealizedPl(Instant from) (defined in src/main/java/pro/mrpc/mt4/MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Per open order, the maximum favorable (max_unrealized_pl) and maximum adverse (min_unrealized_pl) floating P/L reached since it opened, each with a timestamp.
  • Why you need it. MFE/MAE analysis — how far trades run in your favor before you exit, and how deep they dip before recovering.
  • When to use. Tuning stop-loss / take-profit placement and trailing logic from real behaviour.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• See the peak profit each open order reached (MFE)
  • See the deepest drawdown each open order survived (MAE)
  • Timestamps of both extrema (server and UTC)
  • Drive data-informed SL/TP and trailing decisions

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public TradeUnrealizedPLData tradeUnrealizedPl(Instant from)

from is an optional UTC java.time.Instant (pass null for full history); it is sent as an ISO-8601 string.

Request message:

message TradeUnrealizedPLRequest {
  string from = 1;       // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  string from_utc = 2;   // ISO-8601 start in UTC
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message TradeUnrealizedPLData {
  repeated TradeUnrealizedExtremaData extrema = 1;
}

message TradeUnrealizedExtremaData {
  int64 ticket = 1;
  string symbol = 2;
  Timestamp max_unrealized_time = 3;      // when peak profit was reached
  double max_unrealized_pl = 4;           // MFE — best floating P/L
  Timestamp min_unrealized_time = 5;      // when deepest loss was reached
  double min_unrealized_pl = 6;           // MAE — worst floating P/L
  Timestamp max_unrealized_time_utc = 7;
  Timestamp min_unrealized_time_utc = 8;
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• MFE vs MAE. getMaxUnrealizedPl() is how good the trade got (Maximum Favorable Excursion); getMinUnrealizedPl() is how bad it got (Maximum Adverse Excursion). Both are floating values seen while the order was open, not the realized result.
  • Use it to size stops. If winners routinely dip to −15 pips (MAE) before running, a −10 pip stop was too tight. If MFE far exceeds your actual exits, your TP is leaving money on the table.
  • Signs matter. max_unrealized_pl is usually ≥ 0 and min_unrealized_pl usually ≤ 0, but a trade that was never in profit can have a negative MFE — don't assume positivity.
  • Timestamps are protobuf Timestamps — convert with Instant.ofEpochSecond(ts.getSeconds(), ts.getNanos()).
  • from scopes the set; pass null for everything available.

docs.title: 1) MFE / MAE table
docs.text:
Show, per order, how far it ran in your favor and how deep it dipped.

static void excursionTable(MT4Account account) {
    var data = account.tradeUnrealizedPl(null);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10s %-8s %10s %10s%n", "Ticket", "Symbol", "MFE", "MAE");
    for (var e : data.getExtremaList()) {
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10d %-8s %10.2f %10.2f%n",
                e.getTicket(), e.getSymbol(), e.getMaxUnrealizedPl(), e.getMinUnrealizedPl());
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Were my stops too tight?
docs.text:
Find winners that first went underwater — their MAE tells you the stop distance they actually needed.

static void stopPressure(MT4Account account, double threshold) {
    var deep = new ArrayList<>(account.tradeUnrealizedPl(null).getExtremaList());
    deep.removeIf(e -> e.getMinUnrealizedPl() > threshold);
    deep.sort(Comparator.comparingDouble(e -> e.getMinUnrealizedPl())); // deepest first
    System.out.printf("%d order(s) dipped below %.2f before now:%n", deep.size(), threshold);
    for (var e : deep.subList(0, Math.min(10, deep.size()))) {
        var when = Instant.ofEpochSecond(e.getMinUnrealizedTime().getSeconds());
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "  #%d %s: MAE %.2f at %s%n",
                e.getTicket(), e.getSymbol(), e.getMinUnrealizedPl(), when);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Profit give-back detector
docs.text:
Highlight orders that reached a solid peak — candidates where a trailing stop or earlier TP would have locked in more.

static void giveback(MT4Account account, double minPeak) {
    for (var e : account.tradeUnrealizedPl(null).getExtremaList()) {
        if (e.getMaxUnrealizedPl() >= minPeak) {
            System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "#%d %s: peaked at %.2f (worst %.2f) — review exit/trailing%n",
                    e.getTicket(), e.getSymbol(), e.getMaxUnrealizedPl(), e.getMinUnrealizedPl());
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Open orders only. These extrema describe currently-open orders' journey so far; for closed-trade results use ordersHistory or tradeStats.
  • Floating, not realized. A high MFE doesn't mean you captured it — that's exactly the point of the give-back check.
  • Empty when flat. With no open orders, extrema is empty — handle the zero case.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• With open orders. getExtremaCount() > 0; for each entry max_unrealized_pl >= min_unrealized_pl.
  • Flat account. Returns an empty extrema list without error.
  • Timestamp sanity. min_unrealized_time / max_unrealized_time convert to instants that fall after the order's open time.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market and pending in one list. order_type tells them apart: OO_OP_BUY/OO_OP_SELL are filled market orders; the *LIMIT/*STOP variants are resting pending orders.
  • Buy vs sell side. Buy side = OO_OP_BUY, OO_OP_BUYLIMIT, OO_OP_BUYSTOP; the odd values (1,3,5) are the sell side.
  • OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT are bookkeeping records, not tradable orders — skip them when summing exposure.
  • profit is floating and excludes swap/commision; add them for the true carry cost.
  • Proto spelling: the commission field is commision (single s) → getter getCommision() — use it as-is.
  • Lightweight alternative: opened_orders_tickets returns just ticket numbers for fast polling.

docs.title: 1) Open orders table
docs.text:
Print a readable snapshot of everything currently open.

static String typeLabel(OpenedOrderType t) {
    return switch (t) {
        case OO_OP_BUY -> "BUY";            case OO_OP_SELL -> "SELL";
        case OO_OP_BUYLIMIT -> "BUY LIMIT"; case OO_OP_SELLLIMIT -> "SELL LIMIT";
        case OO_OP_BUYSTOP -> "BUY STOP";   case OO_OP_SELLSTOP -> "SELL STOP";
        default -> "?";
    };
}

static void printOpen(MT4Account account) {
    var data = account.openedOrders();
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10s %-8s %-10s %6s %10s %10s%n", "Ticket", "Symbol", "Type", "Lots", "Price", "Profit");
    double total = 0;
    for (var o : data.getOrderInfosList()) {
        total += o.getProfit();
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%10d %-8s %-10s %6.2f %10.5f %10.2f%n",
                o.getTicket(), o.getSymbol(), typeLabel(o.getOrderType()), o.getLots(), o.getOpenPrice(), o.getProfit());
    }
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "total floating: %+.2f%n", total);
}

docs.title: 2) Only my bot's orders
docs.text:
Filter by magic_number to isolate orders a given strategy opened.

static List<OpenedOrderInfo> myOrders(MT4Account account, int magic) {
    var mine = account.openedOrders().getOrderInfosList().stream()
            .filter(o -> o.getMagicNumber() == magic).toList();
    double floating = mine.stream().mapToDouble(o -> o.getProfit() + o.getSwap() + o.getCommision()).sum();
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "magic %d: %d order(s), net %+.2f%n", magic, mine.size(), floating);
    return mine;
}

docs.title: 3) Net exposure per symbol
docs.text:
Aggregate signed lots per symbol to see your real directional exposure (market orders only).

static Map<String, Double> netExposure(MT4Account account) {
    var net = new TreeMap<String, Double>();
    for (var o : account.openedOrders().getOrderInfosList()) {
        if (o.getOrderType() == OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY)
            net.merge(o.getSymbol(), o.getLots(), Double::sum);
        else if (o.getOrderType() == OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELL)
            net.merge(o.getSymbol(), -o.getLots(), Double::sum);
    }
    net.forEach((sym, lots) -> {
        String side = lots > 0 ? "long" : lots < 0 ? "short" : "flat";
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-8s %+.2f lots (%s)%n", sym, lots, side);
    });
    return net;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pending orders have no profit yet. A *LIMIT/*STOP order isn't filled — its profit is 0; don't count it as exposure.
  • Skip balance/credit rows. OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT appear here but aren't trades — exclude them from lot/exposure math.
  • SL/TP of 0 means "unset", not a price of zero.
  • Snapshot. The list reflects the moment of the call; use on_opened_orders_tickets to react to changes live.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat account. order_infos is empty; the table prints a zero total without error.
  • With a market order open. The new ticket appears with order_type == OO_OP_BUY/OO_OP_SELL and a sensible open_price.
  • Magic filter. Open two orders with different magics and assert myOrders() returns only the matching one.

  • Set math is your friend. Convert to a Set<Integer> to diff against a previous poll and spot what opened or closed.
  • Fetch detail on change only. Poll this; when the set changes, call opened_orders once to get the new details — far cheaper than pulling full detail every tick.

docs.title: 1) Is anything open?
docs.text:
A one-liner liveness/exposure check.

static boolean hasOpenOrders(MT4Account account) {
    return account.openedOrdersTickets().getTicketsCount() > 0;
}

docs.title: 2) Detect opened / closed between polls
docs.text:
Diff two snapshots to react only when the set of open orders changes.

static void watchChanges(MT4Account account, long intervalMs) throws InterruptedException {
    Set<Integer> prev = Set.of();
    while (true) {
        Set<Integer> now = new HashSet<>(account.openedOrdersTickets().getTicketsList());
        var opened = new TreeSet<>(now); opened.removeAll(prev);
        var closed = new TreeSet<>(prev); closed.removeAll(now);
        if (!opened.isEmpty()) System.out.println("opened: " + opened);
        if (!closed.isEmpty()) System.out.println("closed: " + closed);
        prev = now;
        Thread.sleep(intervalMs);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Poll cheap, fetch detail on change
docs.text:
Only pull full order detail when the ticket set actually changes.

static Set<Integer> refreshOnChange(MT4Account account, Set<Integer> prevTickets) {
    Set<Integer> now = new HashSet<>(account.openedOrdersTickets().getTicketsList());
    if (!now.equals(prevTickets)) {
        var details = account.openedOrders();     // one detailed call, only when needed
        System.out.printf("%d open order(s) now%n", details.getOrderInfosCount());
    }
    return now;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ids only. No prices, SL/TP or profit here — don't try to make risk decisions from this call alone.
  • Market + pending mixed. The list doesn't tell you which tickets are filled vs resting; use opened_orders for that.
  • Empty when flat. No open orders → empty tickets list.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat account. tickets is empty.
  • After opening an order. The new ticket appears in tickets and matches the ticket returned by order_send.
  • Diff logic. Open then close an order across two polls and assert the change-detector reports it once as opened, once as closed.

static void recentHistory(MT4Account account, int days) {
    Instant end = Instant.now();
    var hist = account.ordersHistory(EnumOrderHistorySortType.HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC,
            end.minus(days, ChronoUnit.DAYS), end, null, null);
    System.out.printf("%d closed order(s) in %dd%n", hist.getTotalCount(), days);
    for (var o : hist.getOrdersInfoList().stream().limit(20).toList()) {
        String side = o.getOrderType() == OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY ? "BUY" : "SELL";
        double net = o.getProfit() + o.getSwap() + o.getCommision();
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "  #%d %-8s %-4s %.2f %.5f->%.5f  net=%+.2f%n",
                o.getTicket(), o.getSymbol(), side, o.getLots(), o.getOpenPrice(), o.getClosePrice(), net);
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Realized P/L and win rate for a window
docs.text:
static double windowPnl(MT4Account account, int days) {
    Instant end = Instant.now();
    var trades = account.ordersHistory(EnumOrderHistorySortType.HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC,
            end.minus(days, ChronoUnit.DAYS), end, null, null).getOrdersInfoList();
    double realized = trades.stream().mapToDouble(o -> o.getProfit() + o.getSwap() + o.getCommision()).sum();
    long wins = trades.stream().filter(o -> o.getProfit() + o.getSwap() + o.getCommision() > 0).count();
    double wr = trades.isEmpty() ? 0.0 : wins * 100.0 / trades.size();
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%d trades | realized %+.2f | win rate %.1f%%%n", trades.size(), realized, wr);
    return realized;
}

docs.text:
Use total_count + itemsPerPage to walk every page.

static List<HistoryOrderInfo> allHistory(MT4Account account, int days, int pageSize) {
    Instant end = Instant.now(), start = end.minus(days, ChronoUnit.DAYS);
    var out = new ArrayList<HistoryOrderInfo>();
    int page = 0, total;
    do {
        var res = account.ordersHistory(EnumOrderHistorySortType.HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC,
                start, end, page, pageSize);
        out.addAll(res.getOrdersInfoList());
        total = res.getTotalCount();
        if (res.getOrdersInfoCount() == 0) break;
        page++;
    } while (page * pageSize < total);
    System.out.printf("collected %d / %d orders%n", out.size(), total);
    return out;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Costs are separate. profit excludes swap/commision — add them for the true net.
  • Window required for meaningful results. Without from/to you get the default page, not "everything".
  • Page bounds. Stop when you've collected total_count (or a page comes back empty) to avoid an infinite loop.
  • Proto spelling: commision (single s) → getCommision().

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known window. On a demo account with history, getOrdersInfoCount() <= getTotalCount() and timestamps fall inside [from, to].
  • Round-trip. Open then close an order, then query a window covering now — the ticket appears with a close_time and realized profit.
  • Paging. With itemsPerPage smaller than total_count, concatenated pages equal the full set with no duplicates.

docs.title: Quote
docs.text:
The latest quote for a single symbol — bid, ask, day high/low and timestamp.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quote(String symbol) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: Quote(QuoteRequest) -> QuoteReply
  • Payload: QuoteData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A one-shot price read for one symbol: current bid/ask, session high/low, and the quote time.
  • Why you need it. To read the market before placing or managing an order.
  • When to use. Single reads. For a continuous feed, use on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Current bid / ask for a symbol
  • Session high / low
  • Quote timestamp (server / UTC)
  • Compute spread and check tradability

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public QuoteData quote(String symbol)

Request message:

message QuoteRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
}

Payload message:

message QuoteData {
  string symbol = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  Timestamp date_time = 4;
  double high = 5;      // session high
  double low = 6;       // session low
  Timestamp date_time_utc = 7;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String Symbol name, e.g. "EURUSD".

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description symbol getSymbol() Symbol bid getBid() Current bid (you sell at bid) ask getAsk() Current ask (you buy at ask) high / low getHigh() / getLow() Session high / low date_time / date_time_utc getDateTime() / getDateTimeUtc() Quote time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Spread = ask − bid. In price terms; divide by the symbol's pip size to express it in pips.
  • Buy at ask, sell at bid. A market buy fills near ask, a market sell near bid — the spread is the immediate cost of entry.
  • Time field is date_time (not time) → getDateTime(). It's a protobuf Timestamp — convert with Instant.ofEpochSecond(ts.getSeconds(), ts.getNanos()).
  • One symbol per call. For several symbols use quote_many; for a live stream use on_symbol_tick.
  • Market Watch. If a broker returns no price, the symbol may need selecting first — see symbol_select.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
static QuoteData showQuote(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    double spread = q.getAsk() - q.getBid();
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: bid=%.5f ask=%.5f spread=%.5f%n", q.getSymbol(), q.getBid(), q.getAsk(), spread);
    return q;
}

docs.title: 2) Only trade when the spread is tight
docs.text:
A guard you call before entering — skip entries when the spread is abnormally wide (news, illiquid hours).

static boolean spreadOk(MT4Account account, String symbol, double maxSpread) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    double spread = q.getAsk() - q.getBid();
    if (spread > maxSpread) {
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: spread %.5f > %.5f — skip entry%n", symbol, spread, maxSpread);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

docs.title: 3) Where is price in today's range?
docs.text:
Position the current mid inside the session high/low (0% = low, 100% = high).

static double rangePosition(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    double mid = (q.getBid() + q.getAsk()) / 2;
    double span = q.getHigh() - q.getLow();
    double pct = span > 0 ? (mid - q.getLow()) / span * 100 : 0.0;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: mid=%.5f in [%.5f, %.5f] -> %.0f%% of range%n",
            symbol, mid, q.getLow(), q.getHigh(), pct);
    return pct;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not a stream. The quote is the price at call time; don't poll it in a tight loop — use on_symbol_tick for live updates.
  • Spread is in price units. Convert to pips with the symbol's pip size (see symbol_params_many) before comparing across symbols.
  • Unselected symbols. Some brokers return an error/empty price until the symbol is in Market Watch.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. ask >= bid, both positive; low <= bid <= high (roughly) during the session.
  • Unknown symbol. A bogus name surfaces an ApiExceptionMT4, not a silent zero.
  • Spread gate. spreadOk() returns false for a tiny maxSpread and true for a generous one.

docs.title: Quote History (OHLC)
docs.text:
OHLC bar history for a symbol and timeframe over a time range — candles for charts, indicators and backtests.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quoteHistory(String symbol, ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME timeframe, Instant from, Instant to) (defined in MT4Account.java)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A list of OHLC bars for one symbol at a chosen timeframe, between from and to.
  • Why you need it. Charting, indicators (SMA/ATR/…), and backtests.
  • When to use. Any analysis that needs candles rather than a single live price.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• OHLC bars for a timeframe (M1 … MN1)
  • Bounded by a from/to time range
  • Tick volume and spread per bar
  • Feed indicators, charts and backtests

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• from / to are required Instants (UTC) — the range bounds how many bars you get back.
  • tick_volume vs real_volume. On FX most brokers report tick volume; real_volume is often 0.
  • Bars are time-ordered by time; index is their position in the series.
  • For a single live price use quote; for a live stream use on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 1) Fetch the last N hourly bars
docs.text:
static List<HistoryQuote> recentBars(MT4Account account, String symbol, int hours) {
    Instant end = Instant.now();
    var bars = account.quoteHistory(symbol, ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_H1,
            end.minus(hours, ChronoUnit.HOURS), end).getHistoricalQuotesList();
    System.out.printf("%d H1 bars%n", bars.size());
    for (var b : bars.subList(Math.max(0, bars.size() - 3), bars.size())) {
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "  O=%.5f H=%.5f L=%.5f C=%.5f vol=%d%n",
                b.getOpen(), b.getHigh(), b.getLow(), b.getClose(), b.getTickVolume());
    }
    return bars;
}

docs.title: 2) Simple moving average of closes
docs.text:
static Double sma(MT4Account account, String symbol, int period) {
    Instant end = Instant.now();
    var bars = account.quoteHistory(symbol, ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_H1,
            end.minus(period * 2L, ChronoUnit.HOURS), end).getHistoricalQuotesList();
    if (bars.size() < period) return null;
    double value = bars.subList(bars.size() - period, bars.size()).stream()
            .mapToDouble(b -> b.getClose()).average().orElse(0);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "SMA(%d) %s = %.5f%n", period, symbol, value);
    return value;
}

docs.title: 3) Average daily range (last 14 days)
docs.text:
A quick ATR-style volatility read from daily bars.

static double avgDailyRange(MT4Account account, String symbol, int days) {
    Instant end = Instant.now();
    var bars = account.quoteHistory(symbol, ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_D1,
            end.minus(days * 2L, ChronoUnit.DAYS), end).getHistoricalQuotesList();
    var ranges = bars.subList(Math.max(0, bars.size() - days), bars.size());
    double adr = ranges.isEmpty() ? 0.0 : ranges.stream().mapToDouble(b -> b.getHigh() - b.getLow()).average().orElse(0);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "ADR(%d) %s = %.5f%n", days, symbol, adr);
    return adr;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Range too wide. A tight timeframe over a long range returns a lot of bars — scope the window to what you need.
  • Partial last bar. The most recent bar may still be forming; treat it as provisional.
  • Empty result. Weekends/holidays or an out-of-session range can yield few or no bars — guard before indexing.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. H1 over the last 48h returns a sensible bar count with high >= low and low <= close <= high.
  • Ordering. Bars are ascending in time; the last bar's time is close to now.
  • Timeframe scaling. D1 over 14 days returns ~10–14 bars (trading days), far fewer than H1.
