docs.title: Many Quotes
docs.text:
Latest quotes for several symbols in a single round-trip.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quoteMany(List<String> symbols) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: QuoteMany(QuoteManyRequest) -> QuoteManyReply
  • Payload: QuoteManyData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A batch price read — one call returns a QuoteData for each requested symbol.
  • Why you need it. One round-trip for a basket instead of N separate quote calls.
  • When to use. Dashboards, multi-symbol strategies, correlation/spread scans.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Quotes for a list of symbols at once
  • Fewer round-trips than looping quote
  • Same per-symbol fields as a single quote

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public QuoteManyData quoteMany(List<String> symbols)

Request message:

message QuoteManyRequest {
  repeated string symbols = 1;
}

Payload message:

message QuoteManyData {
  repeated QuoteData quotes = 1;   // one QuoteData per symbol
}

message QuoteData {
  string symbol = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  Timestamp date_time = 4;
  double high = 5;
  double low = 6;
  Timestamp date_time_utc = 7;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols List<String> Symbol names, e.g. List.of("EURUSD", "GBPUSD").

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteManyData
docs.text:
Field Java getter Description quotes getQuotesList() / getQuotes(i) / getQuotesCount() One quote per requested symbol

Each QuoteData has getSymbol(), getBid(), getAsk(), getHigh(), getLow(), getDateTime() / getDateTimeUtc() — see quote for the field details.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer this over a loop. For several symbols, one quoteMany beats N quote calls — fewer round-trips and a consistent snapshot.
  • Match by symbol, not position. Index the result by q.getSymbol() rather than assuming the response order matches your request order.
  • Same shape as a single quote — spread is ask − bid, times are protobuf Timestamps.
  • Big baskets. Requesting many symbols is fine, but keep the list to what you actually use.

docs.title: 1) Quote a basket into a map
docs.text:
Index by symbol so lookups are order-independent.

static Map<String, double[]> quoteBasket(MT4Account account, List<String> symbols) {
    var bySymbol = new HashMap<String, double[]>();
    for (var q : account.quoteMany(symbols).getQuotesList())
        bySymbol.put(q.getSymbol(), new double[]{q.getBid(), q.getAsk()});
    for (var sym : symbols) {
        var ba = bySymbol.get(sym);
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-8s bid=%s ask=%s%n", sym,
                ba == null ? "-" : ba[0], ba == null ? "-" : ba[1]);
    }
    return bySymbol;
}

docs.title: 2) Rank symbols by spread
docs.text:
Find which instruments are cheapest/most expensive to enter right now.

static void spreads(MT4Account account, List<String> symbols) {
    account.quoteMany(symbols).getQuotesList().stream()
            .map(q -> Map.entry(q.getSymbol(), q.getAsk() - q.getBid()))
            .sorted(Map.Entry.comparingByValue())
            .forEach(e -> System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-8s spread=%.5f%n", e.getKey(), e.getValue()));
}

docs.title: 3) Refresh a watchlist snapshot
docs.text:
Pull the whole watchlist at once for a dashboard tick.

static final List<String> WATCH = List.of("EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD");

static void watchlist(MT4Account account) {
    for (var q : account.quoteMany(WATCH).getQuotesList()) {
        double mid = (q.getBid() + q.getAsk()) / 2;
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-8s %.5f  (bid %.5f / ask %.5f)%n", q.getSymbol(), mid, q.getBid(), q.getAsk());
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Don't assume order. Map results by q.getSymbol(); the response list may not mirror the request order, and unknown symbols may be omitted.
  • Snapshot, not a stream. For continuous updates use on_symbol_tick with a list of symbols.
  • Spreads differ by symbol. Compare in pips (via symbol_params_many) when ranking across instruments with different pip sizes.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Coverage. Requesting 3 valid symbols returns up to 3 quotes; each symbol is one of those requested.
  • Order-independence. Build the map and assert lookups by name succeed regardless of response order.
  • Parity with single quote. A symbol's quoteMany entry matches a separate quote call taken at the same moment (within tick noise).

docs.title: Server Timezone
docs.text:
The trade server's timezone / UTC offset — align timestamps and sessions to broker time.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.serverTimezone() (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone
  • RPC: ServerTimezone(ServerTimezoneRequest) -> ServerTimezoneReply
  • Payload: ServerTimezoneData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The broker server's UTC offset (and a label/source for it).
  • Why you need it. Server timestamps are in broker time; this lets you convert to/from UTC and reason about trading sessions.
  • When to use. When displaying times, scheduling around sessions, or comparing server time to UTC.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Server UTC offset (seconds)
  • Server/timezone label
  • Source and validation info for the offset

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public ServerTimezoneData serverTimezone()

No arguments.

Request message:

message ServerTimezoneRequest {
}

Payload message:

message ServerTimezoneData {
  string server = 1;                  // server / timezone label
  int32 utc_offset_seconds = 2;       // offset from UTC, in seconds
  SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE source = 3;  // enum: how the offset was determined
  Timestamp validated_utc = 4;        // when the offset was last validated (UTC)
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — ServerTimezoneData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description server getServer() Server / timezone label utc_offset_seconds getUtcOffsetSeconds() Offset from UTC, in seconds (e.g. 3600 = UTC+1) source getSource() How the offset was determined (SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE, see below) validated_utc getValidatedUtc() When the offset was last validated (protobuf Timestamp)

docs.title: SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE — field source
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_UNKNOWN 0 Source not known SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE 1 Offset read live from the server SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LAST_VALIDATED 2 Last validated offset (cached)

Access via Mt4TermApiServerTimezone.SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE.SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Offset is in seconds. Divide by 3600 for hours (e.g. 3600 → UTC+1, 10800 → UTC+3).
  • Server time vs UTC. accountSummary() returns both serverTime and serverTimeUtc; this call gives you the offset to convert any server timestamp yourself.
  • DST. Many FX servers shift with daylight saving — read this at session start rather than hard-coding an offset.
  • Rarely changes within a session — fetch once and cache; refresh daily or on reconnect.

docs.title: 1) Print the server offset
docs.text:
static ServerTimezoneData showTimezone(MT4Account account) {
    var tz = account.serverTimezone();
    double hours = tz.getUtcOffsetSeconds() / 3600.0;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: UTC%+.0f (%ds)  source=%s%n",
            tz.getServer(), hours, tz.getUtcOffsetSeconds(), tz.getSource());
    return tz;
}

docs.title: 2) Convert server time ↔ UTC
docs.text:
Use the offset to turn a server timestamp into UTC (and back).

static Instant serverToUtc(MT4Account account, Instant serverDt) {
    return serverDt.minusSeconds(account.serverTimezone().getUtcOffsetSeconds());
}

static Instant utcToServer(MT4Account account, Instant utcDt) {
    return utcDt.plusSeconds(account.serverTimezone().getUtcOffsetSeconds());
}

docs.title: 3) Is it the weekend (server time)?
docs.text:
Gate trading around the broker's week using server-local time.

static boolean isWeekendServer(MT4Account account) {
    long off = account.serverTimezone().getUtcOffsetSeconds();
    var serverNow = Instant.now().plusSeconds(off).atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC);
    var dow = serverNow.getDayOfWeek();
    return dow == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || dow == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Seconds, not hours. utc_offset_seconds is seconds — convert before formatting.
  • DST drift. Don't cache the offset across days; brokers shift with daylight saving.
  • Session math. Trading sessions and rollover are defined in server time — convert before comparing to UTC schedules.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. utc_offset_seconds is a plausible value (typically a multiple of 1800) and server is non-empty.
  • Consistency. accountSummary().getServerTime() minus getServerTimeUtc() roughly equals utc_offset_seconds.
  • Conversion round-trip. utcToServer(serverToUtc(dt)) returns the original instant.

docs.title: Symbol Parameters

docs.text:
• What it is. The trading specification for symbols — the numbers you need to size, round and validate orders.
  • Why you need it. To normalize volume/price, respect the broker's minimum stop distance, and compute money-per-pip.
  • When to use. Before sizing or sending orders; cache the result and refresh occasionally.

docs.text:
• Volume min / max / step / limit
  • Digits and point size (precision)
  • Stops & freeze levels (minimum SL/TP distance)
  • Tick value / tick size / contract size (P/L math)

docs.text:
public SymbolParamsManyData symbolParamsMany(String symbolName)

Pass a single symbol name; pass null (sent as empty) to fetch all symbols.

Request message:

message SymbolParamsManyRequest {

}

}

SymbolParamsManyInfo has ~75 fields; the trading-relevant ones are below.

docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbolName String, optional Restrict to one symbol; pass null/empty for all symbols.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyData
docs.text:
getSymbolInfosList() / getSymbolInfos(i) / getSymbolInfosCount() — a list of SymbolParamsManyInfo. Key getters:

Identity & precision

Field Java getter Description SymbolName getSymbolName() Symbol name Digits getDigits() Price decimal places Point getPoint() Point size (e.g. 0.00001) SymDescription getSymDescription() Human description Path getPath() Market Watch path/category

Volume (lots)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Stops level is in points, not pips. TradeStopsLevel is the minimum SL/TP distance in points — convert with Point (and remember 1 pip = 10 points on 5-digit symbols).
  • This is the source for normalization. VolumeMin/Max/Step round lots; Digits/Point round prices. MT4Sugar's normalizeLot / normalizePrice are built on these.
  • Request one or all. Pass symbolName for a single symbol; pass null to fetch the whole table (can be large).
  • Cache it. These rarely change intraday — fetch once and reuse, refreshing occasionally.

docs.title: 1) Normalize a lot to the broker's rules
docs.text:
Round any desired volume into the allowed [min, max] range on the correct step.

static double normalizeLot(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var info = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    double step = info.getVolumeStep(), lo = info.getVolumeMin(), hi = info.getVolumeMax();
    lots = Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, lots));
    double steps = Math.round(lots / step);
    return Math.round(steps * step * 1e8) / 1e8;
}
// normalizeLot(account, "EURUSD", 0.0234) -> 0.02

docs.title: 2) Is my SL far enough from price?
docs.text:
Validate a stop distance against TradeStopsLevel before sending an order.

static boolean slDistanceOk(MT4Account account, String symbol, double slDistancePrice) {
    var info = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    double minDistance = info.getTradeStopsLevel() * info.getPoint();
    if (slDistancePrice < minDistance) {
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "SL too close: %.5f < min %.5f%n", slDistancePrice, minDistance);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

docs.title: 3) Money per pip for a lot
docs.text:
Compute the P/L value of one pip for sizing by risk.

static double moneyPerPip(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var info = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    int pipPoints = (info.getDigits() == 3 || info.getDigits() == 5) ? 10 : 1;
    double value = info.getTradeTickValue() * (pipPoints * info.getPoint() / info.getTradeTickSize()) * lots;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: ~%.2f %s per pip for %s lot%n", symbol, value, info.getCurrencyProfit(), lots);
    return value;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Points vs pips. TradeStopsLevel, TradeFreezeLevel and Point are in points; convert to pips before comparing to pip-based SL/TP.
  • TradeStopsLevel may be 0. Some brokers report 0 (no minimum) — your SL/TP can then sit anywhere, but still normalize to Digits.
  • Large payload for "all". Passing null returns every symbol — request one when you only need one.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Single symbol. symbolParamsMany("EURUSD").getSymbolInfos(0) has getSymbolName() == "EURUSD".
  • Normalization. normalizeLot(..., 0.0234) returns a multiple of VolumeStep within [VolumeMin, VolumeMax].
  • All symbols. Passing null returns many entries; each has positive Digits and VolumeStep.

docs.title: Symbol Select (Market Watch)
docs.text:
Add a symbol to, or remove it from, Market Watch.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.symbolSelect(String symbol, boolean select) (defined in MT4Account.java)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Toggle a symbol in the terminal's Market Watch (select = add, deselect = remove).
  • Why you need it. Some brokers won't quote or trade a symbol until it's selected.
  • When to use. Before quoting/trading a symbol that might not be in Market Watch yet.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Add a symbol to Market Watch
  • Remove a symbol from Market Watch
  • Confirm the operation via success

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public SymbolSelectData symbolSelect(String symbol, boolean select)

Request message:

message SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  bool select = 2;     // true = add to Market Watch, false = remove
}

Payload message:

message SymbolSelectData {
  bool success = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String Symbol name. select boolean true to add to Market Watch, false to remove.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolSelectData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description success getSuccess() True if the select/deselect was applied

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select before you quote/trade symbols that aren't in Market Watch — some brokers reject data/orders for unselected symbols.
  • Deselect to tidy up (select = false), but don't remove a symbol that still has open orders or active subscriptions.
  • Idempotent-ish. Selecting an already-selected symbol just returns success = true.
  • Validate the name first with symbols — selecting a non-existent symbol fails.

docs.title: 1) Ensure a symbol is ready to use
docs.text:
A helper to call before quoting/trading an unfamiliar symbol.

static boolean ensureSelected(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    boolean ok = account.symbolSelect(symbol, true).getSuccess();
    if (!ok) System.out.println("could not select " + symbol);
    return ok;
}

// usage:
// if (ensureSelected(account, "XAUUSD")) { var q = account.quote("XAUUSD"); }

docs.title: 2) Add then remove
docs.text:
static void tempSelect(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    account.symbolSelect(symbol, true);
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: bid=%.5f ask=%.5f%n", symbol, q.getBid(), q.getAsk());
    account.symbolSelect(symbol, false);   // tidy up
}

docs.title: 3) Prepare a watchlist
docs.text:
Select everything a strategy needs up front.

static Map<String, Boolean> prepareWatchlist(MT4Account account, List<String> symbols) {
    var ok = new LinkedHashMap<String, Boolean>();
    for (var s : symbols) ok.put(s, account.symbolSelect(s, true).getSuccess());
    var missing = ok.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> !e.getValue()).map(Map.Entry::getKey).toList();
    if (!missing.isEmpty()) System.out.println("failed to select: " + missing);
    return ok;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Invalid symbol. Selecting a name that isn't on the account fails (or raises) — resolve it against symbols first.
  • Don't deselect active symbols. Removing a symbol with open orders or live streams can disrupt them.
  • Selection ≠ data guarantee. success = true means it's in Market Watch; the first quote may still lag a moment while it populates.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Select a valid symbol. Returns success = true; a following quote works.
  • Deselect. select = false returns success = true for a selected symbol.
  • Invalid name. A bogus symbol returns success = false or raises ApiExceptionMT4.

• What it is. Every instrument the broker exposes on this account, as (name, index) pairs.
  • Why you need it. To discover tradable symbols at runtime and validate user input.
  • When to use. On startup, when building symbol pickers, or before quoting/trading an unknown name.

• Full symbol list from the broker
  • Validate a symbol name before using it
  • Build lookups (name → index) for other calls

docs.text:
public SymbolsData symbols()

No arguments.

Request message:

message SymbolsRequest {
}

Payload message:

  repeated SymbolNameInfo SymbolNameInfos = 1;
}

  string symbol_name = 1;

Field Java getter Description SymbolNameInfos getSymbolNameInfosList() / getSymbolNameInfos(i) / getSymbolNameInfosCount() All available symbols

Field Java getter Description symbol_name getSymbolName() Symbol name (e.g. "EURUSD") symbol_index getSymbolIndex() Broker-assigned index

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Field name. The repeated proto field is SymbolNameInfos (PascalCase); the Java getters are the usual getSymbolNameInfos….
  • Names are the broker's. Symbols may carry suffixes (EURUSD.m, EURUSD-ECN) — never assume the bare "EURUSD" exists; check the list.
  • This is the catalog, not the rules. For lot limits, digits and trade mode, use symbol_params_many; for prices, use quote.
  • Market Watch. Some brokers require a symbol be selected before quoting it — see symbol_select.

docs.title: 1) List and count
docs.text:
static List<String> listSymbols(MT4Account account) {
    var names = account.symbols().getSymbolNameInfosList().stream()
            .map(s -> s.getSymbolName()).toList();
    System.out.printf("%d symbols, e.g. %s%n", names.size(), names.subList(0, Math.min(8, names.size())));
    return names;
}

docs.title: 2) Does a symbol exist (allowing suffixes)?
docs.text:
Validate a desired symbol, tolerating broker suffixes.

static String resolveSymbol(MT4Account account, String wanted) {
    var names = account.symbols().getSymbolNameInfosList().stream().map(s -> s.getSymbolName()).toList();
    if (names.contains(wanted)) return wanted;
    var match = names.stream().filter(n -> n.startsWith(wanted)).findFirst();
    if (match.isPresent()) {
        System.out.printf("'%s' not found; using '%s'%n", wanted, match.get());
        return match.get();
    }
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("no symbol matching " + wanted);
}

docs.title: 3) Name → index map
docs.text:
Build a lookup you can reuse elsewhere.

static Map<String, Integer> symbolIndexMap(MT4Account account) {
    var map = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
    for (var s : account.symbols().getSymbolNameInfosList()) map.put(s.getSymbolName(), s.getSymbolIndex());
    return map;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Suffixes. Don't hard-code "EURUSD"; resolve against the real list to survive brokers that use suffixes.
  • Catalog only. No prices or trading rules here — pair with quote / symbol_params_many.
  • Large list. Brokers expose hundreds of symbols; filter to what you need rather than printing everything.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Non-empty. On a connected demo account, the list has many entries and names are unique.
  • Resolution. resolveSymbol("EURUSD") returns a real name present in the list.
  • Map integrity. The name→index map has the same length as the symbol list (no duplicate names).

docs.title: Tick Value & Size
docs.text:
Tick value, tick size and contract size per symbol — the inputs for P/L and risk-based position sizing.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tickValueWithSize(List<String> symbolNames) (defined in MT4Account.java)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. For each requested symbol: the money value of one tick, the price size of one tick, and the contract size (units per lot).
  • Why you need it. To turn pips into money — money-per-pip, P/L estimates, and risk-based lot sizing.
  • When to use. When computing position size from a dollar/percent risk, or valuing a move.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Tick value (money per tick for 1 lot)
  • Tick size (price change of one tick)
  • Contract size (units per lot)
  • Lightweight — just the numbers needed for sizing

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public TickValueWithSizeData tickValueWithSize(List<String> symbolNames)

Request message:

message TickValueWithSizeRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;
}

Payload message:

message TickValueWithSizeData {
  repeated SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo infos = 1;
}

message SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo {
  int32 index = 1;
  string symbolName = 2;
  double TradeTickValue = 3;      // money per tick, 1 lot
  double TradeTickSize = 4;       // price change per tick
  double TradeContractSize = 5;   // units per lot
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbolNames List<String> Symbols to query, e.g. List.of("EURUSD", "XAUUSD").

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — TickValueWithSizeData
docs.text:
getInfosList() / getInfos(i) / getInfosCount() — a list of SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo:

Field Java getter Description symbolName getSymbolName() Symbol (note camelCase) TradeTickValue getTradeTickValue() Money value of one tick, for 1 lot (in deposit currency) TradeTickSize getTradeTickSize() Price change of one tick TradeContractSize getTradeContractSize() Units per lot index getIndex() Position in the request

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• This is the subset of symbol_params_many needed for sizing — use this when you only need the tick/contract numbers for several symbols at once.
  • Money per pip = getTradeTickValue() × (pipSize / getTradeTickSize()), where pipSize is 10 × point on 5/3-digit FX (get Point/Digits from symbol_params_many).
  • Values are per 1 lot in the account's deposit currency — multiply by your lot size.
  • MT4Sugar builds on this for calcLotByRisk / calcCashRisk.

docs.title: 1) Tick value for a basket
docs.text:
static Map<String, SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo> tickValues(MT4Account account, List<String> symbols) {
    var out = new LinkedHashMap<String, SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo>();
    for (var i : account.tickValueWithSize(symbols).getInfosList()) {
        out.put(i.getSymbolName(), i);
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%-8s tick_value=%.5f tick_size=%.5f contract=%.0f%n",
                i.getSymbolName(), i.getTradeTickValue(), i.getTradeTickSize(), i.getTradeContractSize());
    }
    return out;
}

docs.title: 2) Money per pip
docs.text:
Convert tick value to per-pip value (needs the symbol's pip size).

static double moneyPerPip(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var tv = account.tickValueWithSize(List.of(symbol)).getInfos(0);
    var p = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    double pipSize = p.getPoint() * ((p.getDigits() == 3 || p.getDigits() == 5) ? 10 : 1);
    double value = tv.getTradeTickValue() * (pipSize / tv.getTradeTickSize()) * lots;
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: %.2f per pip for %s lot%n", symbol, value, lots);
    return value;
}

docs.title: 3) Risk-based lot size
docs.text:
Size a position so a stop-loss hit costs a fixed amount.

static double lotForRisk(MT4Account account, String symbol, double riskAmount, double slPips) {
    double mpp = moneyPerPip(account, symbol, 1.0);   // per-pip for 1 lot
    if (mpp <= 0 || slPips <= 0) return 0.0;
    double raw = riskAmount / (slPips * mpp);
    var p = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    double lots = Math.max(p.getVolumeMin(), Math.min(p.getVolumeMax(),
            Math.round(raw / p.getVolumeStep()) * p.getVolumeStep()));
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "risk %.2f @ %s pip SL -> %.2f lot%n", riskAmount, slPips, lots);
    return Math.round(lots * 100) / 100.0;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Mixed-case fields. Proto symbolName (camelCase) but TradeTickValue (PascalCase); the Java getters normalize both to getSymbolName() / getTradeTickValue().
  • Per 1 lot. Remember to scale by lot size; the raw values assume one lot.
  • Pip vs tick. Tick ≠ pip. Convert via the symbol's pip size (Point/Digits from symbol_params_many).
  • Deposit currency. TradeTickValue is already in your account currency — no FX conversion needed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known symbol. For EURUSD on a USD account, TradeTickValue ≈ 1.0 for 1 lot at 0.00001 tick size.
  • Batch. Requesting 3 symbols returns up to 3 infos; match by symbolName.
  • Sizing sanity. lotForRisk(risk=50, slPips=50) on EURUSD returns ~0.10 lot (≈ $1/pip) — adjust for the actual tick value.

docs.text: Send market/pending orders, modify SL/TP/price, close or delete, and close-by.

docs.text:

docs.title: ⚠️ Errors are exceptions
docs.text:
MT4 trading calls do not return a numeric result code (that's MT5). On rejection they throw ApiExceptionMT4; inspect e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() / getMqlErrorDescription(). Always wrap trading calls in try/catch.

For pip-based SL/TP, lot/price normalization and risk sizing, prefer the MT4Sugar helpers (buyMarket, buyLimit, modifySlTpByPips, close, …) which wrap these low-level calls.

docs.title: Order Close By
docs.text:
Close an order by an opposite order on the same symbol — net a hedge in one operation.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.orderCloseBy(int ticketToClose, int oppositeTicketClosingBy) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderCloseBy(OrderCloseByRequest) -> OrderCloseByReply
  • Payload: OrderCloseByData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes one order using an opposite-direction order on the same symbol, netting them against each other.
  • Why you need it. To unwind a hedge (a buy and a sell on the same symbol) in a single operation instead of closing each leg.
  • When to use. When you hold opposite orders on one symbol and want to net them.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Close-by between two opposite tickets
  • Net a hedge in one call
  • Get the resulting close price / profit

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public OrderCloseByData orderCloseBy(int ticketToClose, int oppositeTicketClosingBy)

Request message:

message OrderCloseByRequest {
  int32 ticket_to_close = 1;
  int32 opposite_ticket_closing_by = 2;
}

Payload message:

message OrderCloseByData {
  double close_price = 1;
  double profit = 2;
  Timestamp close_time = 3;
  Timestamp close_time_utc = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description ticketToClose int The ticket to be closed. oppositeTicketClosingBy int The opposite-direction ticket used to close it.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseByData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description close_price getClosePrice() Price at which the close-by settled profit getProfit() Realized profit from the operation close_time / close_time_utc getCloseTime() / getCloseTimeUtc() Close time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Both legs must be opposite and same-symbol. A BUY and a SELL on the same instrument; close-by nets them.
  • Order of tickets matters. ticketToClose is the one being closed; oppositeTicketClosingBy is the counter order.
  • Broker support varies. Not all brokers allow close-by (and hedging must be permitted); unsupported setups throw ApiExceptionMT4.
  • Alternative: close each leg independently with order_close_delete if close-by isn't available.
  • Market must be open — a closed session throws ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132).

docs.title: 1) Close one order by another
docs.text:
static OrderCloseByData closeBy(MT4Account account, int ticket, int opposite) {
    var res = account.orderCloseBy(ticket, opposite);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "closed #%d by #%d: profit=%+.2f @ %.5f%n",
            ticket, opposite, res.getProfit(), res.getClosePrice());
    return res;
}

docs.title: 2) Net a hedge on a symbol
docs.text:
Find a buy and a sell on the same symbol and close them against each other.

static OrderCloseByData netHedge(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    var orders = account.openedOrders().getOrderInfosList();
    var buy = orders.stream().filter(o -> o.getSymbol().equals(symbol)
            && o.getOrderType() == OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY).findFirst();
    var sell = orders.stream().filter(o -> o.getSymbol().equals(symbol)
            && o.getOrderType() == OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELL).findFirst();
    if (buy.isPresent() && sell.isPresent()) {
        var res = account.orderCloseBy(buy.get().getTicket(), sell.get().getTicket());
        System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "netted %s: profit=%+.2f%n", symbol, res.getProfit());
        return res;
    }
    System.out.println("no opposite pair on " + symbol);
    return null;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Must be a true opposite pair. Same symbol, opposite directions — otherwise the call is rejected.
  • Hedging may be disabled. Brokers that forbid hedging (or close-by) throw ApiExceptionMT4; fall back to order_close_delete.
  • Market closed. Throws ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132) on a closed session.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Wrap in try/catch.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (market open, hedging allowed). Open a BUY and a SELL 0.01 on one symbol, then orderCloseBy → both leave opened_orders.
  • Unsupported. On a non-hedging broker, assert the call throws rather than silently doing nothing.
  • Result fields. close_price and close_time are populated on success.

• What it is. Closes a filled market order (whole or part) or removes a resting pending order — the server picks the right action by order type.
  • Why you need it. To exit positions, take partial profit, or cancel pendings.
  • When to use. Taking profit/loss, scaling out, or cleanup. MT4Sugar's close / closeAll / cancelPendings wrap this.

• Close a market order in full

public OrderCloseDeleteData orderCloseDelete(
        int orderTicket, Double lots, Double closingPrice, Integer slippage)

Each boxed argument is optional — pass null to omit (lots = null closes in full).

Request message:

message OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
  int32 order_ticket = 1;
  double lots = 2;            // partial close volume; omit for full
  double closing_price = 3;   // market close price (optional)
  int32 slippage = 4;
}

Payload message:

message OrderCloseDeleteData {
  OrderCloseDeleteMode mode = 1;        // which action happened
  string history_order_comment = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description orderTicket int Ticket to close or delete. lots Double, optional Lots to close (partial); pass null to close in full. closingPrice Double, optional Closing price for market orders. slippage Integer, optional Max slippage in points.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description mode getMode() Whether a market order was closed or a pending deleted (OrderCloseDeleteMode) history_order_comment getHistoryOrderComment() Resulting history/close comment

docs.title: OrderCloseDeleteMode — field mode
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning OCD_MARKET_ORDER 0 A market order was closed OCD_PENDING_ORDER 1 A pending order was deleted

Access via Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderCloseDeleteMode.OCD_MARKET_ORDER.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call, both actions. You don't choose close-vs-delete — the server does it based on the order type and reports it in mode.
  • Partial close. Pass lots smaller than the order's volume; the remainder stays open as a separate ticket.
  • Pending deletes ignore lots. For a pending order the whole thing is removed.
  • Market must be open to close a market order — a weekend/closed market throws ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132).
  • Bulk exits. For closing many orders use MT4Sugar's closeAll / cancelPendings rather than looping this by hand.

docs.title: 1) Close an order in full
docs.text:
static OrderCloseDeleteData close(MT4Account account, int ticket) {
    var res = account.orderCloseDelete(ticket, null, null, null);
    String kind = res.getMode() == OrderCloseDeleteMode.OCD_MARKET_ORDER ? "closed market" : "deleted pending";
    System.out.printf("#%d: %s%n", ticket, kind);
    return res;
}

docs.title: 2) Partial close (scale out)
docs.text:
Close half of a position, leaving the rest to run.

static void closeHalf(MT4Account account, int ticket, double lots) {
    double half = Math.round(lots / 2 * 100) / 100.0;
    account.orderCloseDelete(ticket, half, null, null);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "#%d: closed %.2f lot, rest left open%n", ticket, half);
}

docs.title: 3) Close everything on a symbol
docs.text:
Pull open orders, then close each matching ticket.

static void closeSymbol(MT4Account account, String symbol) {
    for (var o : account.openedOrders().getOrderInfosList()) {
        if (o.getSymbol().equals(symbol)) {
            try {
                account.orderCloseDelete(o.getTicket(), null, null, null);
                System.out.println("closed #" + o.getTicket());
            } catch (Exception e) {
                System.out.println("#" + o.getTicket() + " failed: " + e.getMessage());
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Market closed. Closing a market order when the session is closed throws ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132) — pendings can still usually be deleted.
  • Partial close limits. lots must respect the symbol's volume step and be ≤ the order's volume.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Failures throw ApiExceptionMT4; wrap in try/catch.
  • Already closed. Closing a ticket that's gone throws — tolerate it in cleanup loops.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Round-trip (market open). order_send then orderCloseDelete → mode == OCD_MARKET_ORDER; the ticket leaves opened_orders.
  • Pending delete. Place a pending order and delete it → mode == OCD_PENDING_ORDER.
  • Partial. Close part of a 0.02 position and assert a 0.01 remainder stays open.

docs.title: Order Modify
docs.text:
Change an existing order's SL, TP, pending price or expiration.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.orderModify(int orderTicket, Double newPrice, Double newStopLoss, Double newTakeProfit, Instant newExpiration) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) -> OrderModifyReply
  • Payload: OrderModifyData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Updates SL/TP (and, for pending orders, the entry price / expiration) of an order that already exists.
  • Why you need it. To manage live orders without closing them — trailing stops, breakeven, re-pricing pendings.
  • When to use. Any time you adjust protection or a pending price. MT4Sugar's modifySlTpByPrice / modifySlTpByPips wrap this.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Change SL / TP on a live order
  • Re-price a pending order
  • Update a pending order's expiration

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public OrderModifyData orderModify(
        int orderTicket,
        Double newPrice, Double newStopLoss, Double newTakeProfit,
        Instant newExpiration)

Each Double/Instant argument is optional — pass null to leave that field unchanged.

Request message:

message OrderModifyRequest {
  int32 order_ticket = 1;
  double new_price = 2;              // pending-order price
  double new_stop_loss = 3;
  double new_take_profit = 4;
  Timestamp new_expiration = 5;
  Timestamp new_expiration_utc = 6;
}

Payload message:

message OrderModifyData {
  bool order_was_modified = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description orderTicket int Ticket to modify. newPrice Double, optional New pending-order price (ignored for filled market orders). newStopLoss Double, optional New SL price. newTakeProfit Double, optional New TP price. newExpiration Instant, optional New expiration (pending orders).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Field Java getter Description order_was_modified getOrderWasModified() True if the change was applied

On failure the call throws ApiExceptionMT4 — e.g. ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130) when SL/TP is too close, or ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED (145) when nothing changed or the order is too near market.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prices, not pips. newStopLoss / newTakeProfit are absolute prices — convert from pips yourself (or use MT4Sugar's modifySlTpByPips).
  • Pass only what changes. Supply just the fields you want to update; leave the rest null.
  • Respect the stops level. New SL/TP must be at least TradeStopsLevel points from price (symbol_params_many).
  • Pending vs market. newPrice/newExpiration only make sense for pending orders; for filled market orders, modify SL/TP.
  • No-op is an error on some brokers. Submitting unchanged values can throw rather than silently succeed — only call when something actually changes.

docs.title: 1) Set SL and TP on an order
docs.text:
static boolean setStops(MT4Account account, int ticket, double sl, double tp) {
    boolean ok = account.orderModify(ticket, null, sl, tp, null).getOrderWasModified();
    System.out.println(ok ? "modified" : "no change");
    return ok;
}

docs.title: 2) Trail the stop (move SL only)
docs.text:
Raise the stop on a long as price advances — one trailing step.

static void trailStop(MT4Account account, int ticket, String symbol, double distancePips) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    var info = account.symbolParamsMany(symbol).getSymbolInfos(0);
    double pip = info.getPoint() * ((info.getDigits() == 3 || info.getDigits() == 5) ? 10 : 1);
    double scale = Math.pow(10, info.getDigits());
    double newSl = Math.round((q.getBid() - distancePips * pip) * scale) / scale;   // for a BUY
    account.orderModify(ticket, null, newSl, null, null);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "SL -> %.5f%n", newSl);
}

docs.title: 3) Re-price a pending order
docs.text:
Move a resting BUY LIMIT to a new level.

static boolean repricePending(MT4Account account, int ticket, double newPrice) {
    double p = Math.round(newPrice * 1e5) / 1e5;
    return account.orderModify(ticket, p, null, null, null).getOrderWasModified();
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Absolute prices. SL/TP/price are prices, not distances — compute them before calling.
  • Too-close stops. Violating TradeStopsLevel throws ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • No-change calls. Re-submitting identical values may throw (ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED 145) — guard against it.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Failures throw ApiExceptionMT4; wrap in try/catch.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (market open). Modifying SL/TP of an open order returns getOrderWasModified() == true and the new values show in opened_orders.
  • Too-close SL. A stop inside TradeStopsLevel throws ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • No-op. Re-applying the same SL/TP either returns false or throws — assert your code tolerates both.

docs.title: Order Send
docs.text:
Send a market or pending order — the low-level entry point for opening trades.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.orderSend(OrderSendRequest request) / orderSend(String symbol, OrderSendOperationType type, double volume) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) -> OrderSendReply
  • Payload: OrderSendData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Opens a market order or places a pending order, with optional SL/TP, comment and magic.
  • Why you need it. Full control over every order field at the lowest level.
  • When to use. When you need raw control. For pips-based SL/TP, normalization and risk sizing, prefer MT4Sugar (buyMarket, buyLimit, …) which wraps this.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Open market orders (BUY / SELL)
  • Place pending orders (LIMIT / STOP)
  • Attach SL / TP, comment and magic number
  • Set slippage and pending-order expiration

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
// Full control — build the request yourself:
public OrderSendData orderSend(OrderSendRequest request)

// Convenience — a plain market order:
public OrderSendData orderSend(String symbol, OrderSendOperationType type, double volume)

For SL/TP, price, slippage, comment, magic or expiration, build an OrderSendRequest and use the first overload.

Request message:

message OrderSendRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  OrderSendOperationType operation_type = 2;
  double volume = 3;
  double price = 4;
  int32 slippage = 5;
  double stoploss = 6;
  double takeprofit = 7;
  string comment = 8;
  int32 magic_number = 9;
  Timestamp expiration = 10;
  Timestamp expiration_utc = 11;
}

Payload message:

message OrderSendData {
  int32 ticket = 1;
  double volume = 2;
  double price = 3;
  Timestamp open_time = 4;
  Timestamp open_time_utc = 5;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input (OrderSendRequest builder)
docs.text: Field Builder setter Type Description symbol setSymbol String Symbol name. operation_type setOperationType OrderSendOperationType Buy/sell, market or pending (see enum). volume setVolume double Lots. price setPrice double Entry price — required for pending orders; for market orders it can be omitted. slippage setSlippage int Max slippage in points (market orders). stoploss setStoploss double Stop-loss price (0 / omit for none). takeprofit setTakeprofit double Take-profit price (0 / omit for none). comment setComment String Order comment. magic_number setMagicNumber int Expert/magic id to tag the order. expiration setExpiration Timestamp Expiration for pending orders.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text:
Field Java getter Description ticket getTicket() Ticket of the new order volume getVolume() Filled/placed volume price getPrice() Fill price (market) or pending price open_time / open_time_utc getOpenTime() / getOpenTimeUtc() Open/placement time (server / UTC)

On failure the call throws ApiExceptionMT4 — inspect e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() / getMqlErrorDescription() (see Errors).

docs.title: OrderSendOperationType — field operation_type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning OC_OP_BUY 0 Market buy OC_OP_SELL 1 Market sell OC_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit (pending, below price) OC_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit (pending, above price) OC_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop (pending, above price) OC_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop (pending, below price)

Access via Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market vs pending. OC_OP_BUY/OC_OP_SELL fill immediately (price optional); the *LIMIT/*STOP variants are pending and require price.
  • Absolute SL/TP prices. stoploss/takeprofit are prices, not pip distances. Respect the symbol's TradeStopsLevel (symbol_params_many) or you'll get ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • Normalize first. Round volume to VolumeStep and prices to Digits; MT4Sugar does this automatically.
  • Tag with magic_number. It's how you later identify "my" orders in opened_orders.
  • Returns a ticket on success — there is no numeric returned_code (that's MT5); errors are exceptions.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Examples
docs.text: ⚠️ These place real orders on the connected (demo) account. Use 0.01 lots and clean up.

docs.title: 1) Open a market BUY
docs.text:
static int buy(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var res = account.orderSend(symbol, OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, lots);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "opened #%d %s lot @ %.5f%n", res.getTicket(), res.getVolume(), res.getPrice());
    return res.getTicket();
}

docs.title: 2) Market SELL with SL/TP, comment and magic
docs.text:
static int sellWithStops(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    double sl = Math.round((q.getBid() + 0.0020) * 1e5) / 1e5;   // 20 pips above for a short
    double tp = Math.round((q.getBid() - 0.0030) * 1e5) / 1e5;   // 30 pips below
    var req = Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendRequest.newBuilder()
            .setSymbol(symbol).setOperationType(OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_SELL).setVolume(lots)
            .setStoploss(sl).setTakeprofit(tp).setComment("demo sell").setMagicNumber(777)
            .build();
    var res = account.orderSend(req);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "opened #%d SL=%.5f TP=%.5f%n", res.getTicket(), sl, tp);
    return res.getTicket();
}

docs.title: 3) Place a BUY LIMIT below the market
docs.text:
static int buyLimit(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    var q = account.quote(symbol);
    double price = Math.round((q.getAsk() - 0.0030) * 1e5) / 1e5;   // 30 pips below current ask
    var req = Mt4TermApiTradingHelper.OrderSendRequest.newBuilder()
            .setSymbol(symbol).setOperationType(OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUYLIMIT)
            .setVolume(lots).setPrice(price).build();
    var res = account.orderSend(req);
    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "placed BUY LIMIT #%d @ %.5f%n", res.getTicket(), price);
    return res.getTicket();
}

docs.title: 4) Robust send with error handling
docs.text:
static Integer safeBuy(MT4Account account, String symbol, double lots) {
    try {
        return account.orderSend(symbol, OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, lots).getTicket();
    } catch (ApiExceptionMT4 e) {
        int code = e.getError() != null ? e.getError().getMqlErrorIntCode() : -1;
        switch (code) {
            case 134 -> System.out.println("not enough money");       // ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY
            case 130 -> System.out.println("SL/TP too close to price"); // ERR_INVALID_STOPS
            default  -> System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getMessage() + " (" + code + ")");
        }
        return null;
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pending orders need price. Omitting it for a *LIMIT/*STOP order fails.
  • SL/TP are prices. And must respect TradeStopsLevel — too-close stops raise ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • Un-normalized volume/price. Values off the broker's step/digits are rejected (ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME 131 / ERR_INVALID_PRICE 129).
  • Rejections are exceptions, not a return code — always wrap trading calls in try/catch (ApiExceptionMT4).
  • Clean up demos. Close what you open with order_close_delete.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo). A 0.01 market BUY returns a positive ticket; the ticket appears in opened_orders.
  • Round-trip. Open then order_close_delete the ticket; it leaves opened_orders.
  • Failure path. Send an oversized volume and assert ApiExceptionMT4 with a sensible mql_error_int_code.

docs.title: 5. Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text: Real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, ticket lists, open-order profit and connection state.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• Symbol Tick Stream — Subscribe to real-time tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols.
  • Trade Events Stream — Subscribe to trade events (orders opened, updated, removed).
  • Opened Order Tickets Stream — Poll-stream the live lists of open position & pending-order tickets.
  • Open-Order Profit Stream — Stream open-order profit/loss updates (plus an account snapshot).
  • Connection State Stream — Subscribe to terminal connection-state changes.

The first four live on mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService; onConnectState lives on mt4_term_api.Connection.

docs.title: The Java streaming model
docs.text:
Unlike the blocking request methods, every on… call is callback-based:

Subscription onSymbolTick(List<String> symbols,
                          Consumer<OnSymbolTickData> onData,
                          Consumer<Throwable> onError)
  • It returns a MT4Account.Subscription (an AutoCloseable). The stream runs on a background thread and invokes onData for each message.
  • Stop it by closing the subscription — ideally with try-with-resources:
try (MT4Account.Subscription s = account.onSymbolTick(List.of("EURUSD"), d -> {
        var t = d.getSymbolTick();
        System.out.printf("%s %.5f/%.5f%n", t.getSymbol(), t.getBid(), t.getAsk());
    }, err -> System.out.println("stream error: " + err.getMessage()))) {
    Thread.sleep(10_000);   // consume for 10 s, then close() cancels the stream
}
  • Auto-reconnect is built in — a transient gRPC drop reopens the stream and keeps delivering to your callback.
  • onError is called for terminal errors; a null error consumer is allowed (errors are then swallowed after reconnect attempts).

This is the Java analogue of PyMT4's async generators + cancellation_event: onData replaces async for, and Subscription.close() replaces setting the cancellation event. See Streams.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text:
Method What it does onSymbolTick(symbols, onData, onError) Real-time tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols. onTrade(onData, onError) Trade events (orders opened, updated, removed). onOpenedOrdersTickets(pullIntervalMs, onData, onError) Live lists of open position & pending-order tickets. onOpenedOrdersProfit(timerPeriodMs, onData, onError) Open-order profit/loss updates (plus an account snapshot). onConnectState(terminalIds, onData, onError) Terminal connection-state changes.
  • Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Connection State Stream
docs.text:
A live stream of terminal connection-state changes.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.onConnectState(List<String> terminalIds, Consumer<ConnectStateData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • RPC: OnConnectState(OnConnectStateRequest) -> stream of OnConnectStateReply
  • Payload: ConnectStateData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A subscription that delivers the terminal's connection state — connected/alive flags, server and account, with a timestamp.
  • Why you need it. To react to connectivity changes (drops, recoveries) for health monitoring and auto-recovery.
  • When to use. Supervising a long-running bot. Close the Subscription to stop.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Connected / alive flags for the terminal session
  • Server and account context
  • Event timestamps and any error message

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public Subscription onConnectState(
        List<String> terminalIds,
        Consumer<ConnectStateData> onData,
        Consumer<Throwable> onError)

Pass null (or an empty list) for terminalIds to watch the current session.

Request message:

message OnConnectStateRequest {
  repeated string terminal_ids = 1;   // omit for the current session
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message ConnectStateData {
  string id = 1;
  string state = 2;            // e.g. "Connected"
  bool is_connected = 3;
  bool is_alive = 4;
  bool api_is_alive = 5;
  string server = 6;
  uint64 account = 7;
  string error_message = 8;
  Timestamp timestamp = 9;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description terminalIds List<String>, optional Restrict to specific terminal ids; pass null for the current session. onData Consumer<ConnectStateData> Called on each state update. onError Consumer<Throwable> Called on a terminal stream error (may be null).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — onData receives ConnectStateData
docs.text: Field Java getter Description state getState() State label (e.g. "Connected") is_connected getIsConnected() Session is connected to the server is_alive getIsAlive() Terminal is alive api_is_alive getApiIsAlive() API layer is alive server getServer() Server name account getAccount() Account login error_message getErrorMessage() Error text, if any timestamp getTimestamp() Event time id getId() Terminal/session id

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• state is a string, not an enum — compare against labels like "Connected", or rely on the getIsConnected() / getIsAlive() booleans.
  • Three liveness flags. isConnected (to the broker), isAlive (terminal), apiIsAlive (gateway) — a healthy session has all three true.
  • Check errorMessage when a flag flips false — it carries the reason.
  • Works regardless of market hours — it reports session health, not prices.
  • Close to stop the subscription — see Streams.

docs.title: 1) Watch connection state
docs.text:
static Subscription watchState(MT4Account account) {
    return account.onConnectState(null, ev ->
            System.out.printf("%s connected=%s alive=%s server=%s%n",
                    ev.getState(), ev.getIsConnected(), ev.getIsAlive(), ev.getServer()), null);
}

docs.title: 2) Wait until connected
docs.text:
Block until the session reports a healthy state (with a timeout).

static boolean waitConnected(MT4Account account, long timeoutMs) throws InterruptedException {
    var ok = new CountDownLatch(1);
    try (var s = account.onConnectState(null, ev -> {
            if (ev.getIsConnected() && ev.getIsAlive()) ok.countDown();
        }, null)) {
        return ok.await(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Alert on disconnect
docs.text:
Fire a callback the moment connectivity drops.

static Subscription onDisconnect(MT4Account account, BiConsumer<String, String> callback) {
    return account.onConnectState(null, ev -> {
        if (!ev.getIsConnected() || !ev.getIsAlive())
            callback.accept(ev.getState(), ev.getErrorMessage());
    }, null);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• state is free-form text. Prefer the boolean flags over string matching where possible.
  • No close = leak. Stop by closing the Subscription.
  • Events are sparse. State is reported on change/heartbeat — don't expect a steady stream; use a timeout when waiting.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Healthy session. Shortly after connecting, an event has state == "Connected" with all three liveness flags true.
  • waitConnected. Returns true on a live demo session within the timeout.
  • Clean stop. Closing the Subscription ends delivery without leaking threads.

docs.title: Open-Order Profit Stream
docs.text:
A live P/L ticker for open orders, emitted on a timer — plus an account snapshot.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(int timerPeriodMilliseconds, Consumer<OnOpenedOrdersProfitData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService

  • Payload: OnOpenedOrdersProfitData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Every timerPeriodMilliseconds it delivers the current floating P/L of each open order.
  • Why you need it. Real-time floating P/L without polling — risk dashboards, trailing/exit logic.
  • When to use. Live P/L monitoring and profit-target automation. Close the Subscription to stop.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Per-order live profit
  • Emission interval control
  • Account snapshot alongside each update

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public Subscription onOpenedOrdersProfit(
        int timerPeriodMilliseconds,
        Consumer<OnOpenedOrdersProfitData> onData,
        Consumer<Throwable> onError)

Request message:

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest {

}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitData {
  MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type = 1;
  repeated OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo opened_orders_with_profit_updated = 2;

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo {

  double order_profit = 10;
  double stop_loss = 11;

}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Profit field is order_profit (getOrderProfit()), not profit, on these items.
  • Timer-driven. Updates arrive on timerPeriodMilliseconds, independent of ticks — so you get P/L updates even between price changes.
  • Same operation enum as on_trade. Order type is SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (SUB_OP_*).
  • Works on a closed market (it re-values current orders on a timer), though P/L won't move without price changes.
  • Close to stop the subscription — see Streams.

docs.title: 1) Live P/L per order
docs.text:
static Subscription livePnl(MT4Account account) {
    return account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(1000, ev -> {
        for (var o : ev.getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList())
            System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "#%d %s %+.2f%n", o.getTicket(), o.getSymbol(), o.getOrderProfit());
    }, null);
}

docs.title: 2) Alert on total floating loss
docs.text:
Stop and alert when aggregate floating P/L breaches a limit.

static boolean floatingGuard(MT4Account account, double maxLoss, long timeoutMs) throws InterruptedException {
    var breached = new CountDownLatch(1);
    try (var s = account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(2000, ev -> {
            double total = ev.getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList().stream()
                    .mapToDouble(o -> o.getOrderProfit()).sum();
            System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "floating: %+.2f%n", total);
            if (total <= maxLoss) {
                System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "[ALERT] floating %.2f <= %.2f — de-risk!%n", total, maxLoss);
                breached.countDown();
            }
        }, null)) {
        return breached.await(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Close an order when it hits a profit target
docs.text:
Watch the stream and close the ticket once its profit reaches the target.

static void takeProfitAt(MT4Account account, int ticket, double target, long timeoutMs) throws InterruptedException {
    var done = new CountDownLatch(1);
    try (var s = account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(1000, ev -> {
            for (var o : ev.getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList()) {
                if (o.getTicket() == ticket && o.getOrderProfit() >= target) {
                    account.orderCloseDelete(ticket, null, null, null);
                    System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "#%d hit %.2f -> closed%n", ticket, target);
                    done.countDown();
                }
            }
        }, null)) {
        done.await(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Field is order_profit. Not profit — use getOrderProfit().
  • No close = leak. Stop by closing the Subscription.
  • Acting inside the callback. Closing/modifying from within the stream is fine, but keep per-update work light.
  • Flat account. With nothing open, opened_orders_with_profit_updated is empty.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• With open orders. Each update lists your open tickets; order_profit moves with price.
  • Total. Summed order_profit roughly matches equity − balance from account_summary.
  • Clean stop. Closing the Subscription ends delivery without leaking threads.

docs.title: Opened Order Tickets Stream
docs.text:
A periodic stream of the live open ticket lists — positions and pending orders.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.onOpenedOrdersTickets(int pullIntervalMilliseconds, Consumer<OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnOpenedOrdersTickets(OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> stream of OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Payload: OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A lightweight heartbeat: every pullIntervalMilliseconds it delivers the current lists of open position and pending-order tickets.
  • Why you need it. Cheap "what's open now?" monitoring without pulling full order detail.
  • When to use. Change detection and liveness. For full detail fetch opened_orders when something changes.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Separate position and pending ticket lists
  • Server-side sampling interval
  • Minimal payload for monitoring loops

docs.text:

Request message:

message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {
  int32 pull_interval_milliseconds = 1;
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

  repeated int32 position_tickets = 1;
  repeated int32 pending_order_tickets = 2;
  Timestamp server_time = 3;

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Positions and pendings are split here — unlike the one-shot opened_orders_tickets, which returns a single flat list.
  • Tune pullIntervalMilliseconds. 500 ms is responsive; raise it (e.g. 2000) to reduce chatter for slow strategies.
  • Fetch detail on change. When a ticket set changes, call opened_orders once — don't stream full detail.
  • Close to stop the subscription — see Streams.
  • This heartbeat works even on a closed market (it samples current state, not ticks).

docs.title: 1) Heartbeat of open tickets
docs.text:
static Subscription heartbeat(MT4Account account) {
    return account.onOpenedOrdersTickets(1000, ev ->
            System.out.printf("positions=%s pending=%s%n",
                    ev.getPositionTicketsList(), ev.getPendingOrderTicketsList()), null);
}

docs.title: 2) Detect opened / closed positions
docs.text:
Diff successive samples and act only on change.

static Subscription watchPositions(MT4Account account) {
    var prev = new AtomicReference<Set<Integer>>(Set.of());
    return account.onOpenedOrdersTickets(1000, ev -> {
        var now = new HashSet<>(ev.getPositionTicketsList());
        if (!now.equals(prev.get())) {
            var opened = new TreeSet<>(now); opened.removeAll(prev.get());
            var closed = new TreeSet<>(prev.get()); closed.removeAll(now);
            System.out.println("opened: " + opened + " closed: " + closed);
            prev.set(now);
        }
    }, null);
}

docs.title: 3) React when a pending order appears
docs.text:
static boolean waitForPending(MT4Account account, long timeoutMs) throws InterruptedException {
    var found = new CountDownLatch(1);
    try (var s = account.onOpenedOrdersTickets(500, ev -> {
            if (ev.getPendingOrderTicketsCount() > 0) found.countDown();
        }, null)) {
        return found.await(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ids only. No prices/profit here — fetch opened_orders for detail.
  • No close = leak. Stop by closing the Subscription.
  • Interval trade-off. Too small a pullIntervalMilliseconds is chatty; too large is laggy — tune to your needs.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Existing orders. With open orders, position_tickets matches the one-shot opened_orders_tickets.
  • Change detection. Open then close an order and assert the diff reports it once opened, once closed.
  • Clean stop. Closing the Subscription ends delivery without leaking threads.

docs.title: Symbol Tick Stream
docs.text:
A live stream of tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.onSymbolTick(List<String> symbols, Consumer<OnSymbolTickData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) -> stream of OnSymbolTickReply
  • Payload: OnSymbolTickData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A subscription that calls your onData with a tick every time the price of a subscribed symbol changes.
  • Why you need it. To react to price in real time instead of polling quote.
  • When to use. Live strategies, dashboards, spread/price monitors. Close the Subscription to stop.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Live bid/ask per symbol
  • Subscribe to several symbols in one stream
  • Clean stop via Subscription.close()

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public Subscription onSymbolTick(
        List<String> symbols,
        Consumer<OnSymbolTickData> onData,
        Consumer<Throwable> onError)

Returns a MT4Account.Subscription (AutoCloseable). Close it to stop the stream.

Request message:

message OnSymbolTickRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;
}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message OnSymbolTickData {
  OnSymbolMqlTickInfo symbol_tick = 1;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 2;
}

message OnSymbolMqlTickInfo {
  Timestamp time = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  double last = 4;
  uint64 volume = 5;
  int64 time_msc = 6;
  string symbol = 7;
  Timestamp time_utc = 8;
  int64 time_msc_utc = 9;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols List<String> Symbols to subscribe to. onData Consumer<OnSymbolTickData> Called for each tick. onError Consumer<Throwable> Called on a terminal stream error (may be null).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — onData receives OnSymbolTickData
docs.text:
Each item has getSymbolTick() (OnSymbolMqlTickInfo):

Field Java getter Description symbol getSymbol() Symbol bid / ask getBid() / getAsk() Current bid / ask last getLast() Last price (if provided) volume getVolume() Tick volume time / time_utc getTime() / getTimeUtc() Tick time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One callback per tick. Each onData call is one tick for one of the subscribed symbols — check tick.getSymbol() to tell them apart.
  • Close to stop. Use try-with-resources or call subscription.close(), otherwise the stream (and its reconnect loop) keeps running — see Streams.
  • Auto-reconnect. Transient gRPC drops are retried under the hood; your onData keeps firing across a reconnect.
  • No ticks on a closed market. On weekends/holidays the stream stays open but delivers nothing.
  • For a one-shot price use quote; for several at once quote_many.

docs.title: 1) Stream N ticks then stop
docs.text:
static void firstTicks(MT4Account account, String symbol, int n) throws InterruptedException {
    var latch = new CountDownLatch(n);
    try (var s = account.onSymbolTick(List.of(symbol), d -> {
            var t = d.getSymbolTick();
            System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s: bid=%.5f ask=%.5f%n", t.getSymbol(), t.getBid(), t.getAsk());
            latch.countDown();
        }, err -> { while (latch.getCount() > 0) latch.countDown(); })) {
        latch.await(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    }   // close() cancels the stream
}

docs.title: 2) Keep the latest price per symbol
docs.text:
Maintain a live snapshot map you can read from elsewhere.

static Map<String, double[]> livePrices(MT4Account account, List<String> symbols) {
    var latest = new ConcurrentHashMap<String, double[]>();
    account.onSymbolTick(symbols, d -> {
        var t = d.getSymbolTick();
        latest.put(t.getSymbol(), new double[]{t.getBid(), t.getAsk()});
    }, null);   // keep the Subscription if you want to close it later
    return latest;
}

docs.title: 3) Alert on a price level
docs.text:
Close the stream as soon as a target is hit.

static boolean waitForPrice(MT4Account account, String symbol, double target, boolean above, long timeoutMs)
        throws InterruptedException {
    var hit = new CountDownLatch(1);
    try (var s = account.onSymbolTick(List.of(symbol), d -> {
            double bid = d.getSymbolTick().getBid();
            if ((above && bid >= target) || (!above && bid <= target)) {
                System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "%s hit %.5f (bid=%.5f)%n", symbol, target, bid);
                hit.countDown();
            }
        }, null)) {
        return hit.await(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No close = leak. If you never close the Subscription, the stream and its reconnect loop run forever.
  • Blocking on a quiet market. Closed sessions deliver no ticks — use a timeout when awaiting one.
  • Per-tick work must be fast. Heavy processing inside onData backs up the stream — offload to a queue/executor.
  • Distinguish symbols. With multiple symbols, always branch on tick.getSymbol().

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Market open. Subscribing to a liquid symbol delivers ticks within a second; ask >= bid.
  • Clean stop. After close() the callback stops firing promptly without leaking threads.
  • Timeout path. On a closed market, an awaited latch times out rather than hanging forever.

docs.title: Trade Events Stream
docs.text:
A live stream of trade events — orders opened, updated and removed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.onTrade(Consumer<OnTradeData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError) (defined in MT4Account.java)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) -> stream of OnTradeReply
  • Payload: OnTradeData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A subscription that fires whenever an order's lifecycle changes — new, modified, closed/removed.
  • Why you need it. To react instantly to order activity (monitors, copiers, dashboards) instead of polling.
  • When to use. Any event-driven logic around orders. Close the Subscription to stop.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• New / updated / removed order events
  • Per-order operation type (SUB_OP_*)
  • Event group type (profit vs update)
  • Account snapshot alongside each event

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
public Subscription onTrade(Consumer<OnTradeData> onData, Consumer<Throwable> onError)

Request message:

message OnTradeRequest {}

Payload message (field numbers per our stub):

message OnTradeData {
  MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type = 1;
  OnTadeEventData event_data = 2;        // proto spelling: "OnTade…"
  OnEventAccountInfo account_info = 3;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

message OnTadeEventData {
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo new_orders = 1;
  repeated OnTradeUpdatedOrderInfo updated_orders = 2;   // each has previous / current
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo removed_orders = 3;
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo new_history_orders = 4;
}

message OnTradeOrderInfo {
  int32 ticket = 2;
  double lots = 7;
  double open_price = 9;
  double order_profit = 11;
  double stop_loss = 12;
  string symbol = 14;
  double take_profit = 15;
  SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE type = 16;
  // ... index, is_history, comment, commission, magic_number, open_time, swap, close_price, close_time, account_login
}

Each OnTradeOrderInfo carries getTicket(), getSymbol(), getLots(), getOpenPrice(), getStopLoss(), getTakeProfit(), getOrderProfit(), and getType() (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE).

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE — field type
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning OrderProfit 0 Profit-update group OrderUpdate 1 Order lifecycle change

docs.title: SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE — order type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning SUB_OP_BUY 0 Market buy SUB_OP_SELL 1 Market sell SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit SUB_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop SUB_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop

Access via Mt4TermApiSubscriptions.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUY and …MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE.OrderUpdate.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Four buckets per event. event_data splits changes into newOrders, updatedOrders, removedOrders, newHistoryOrders — iterate the ones you care about.
  • Updates carry before/after. Each updatedOrders item has getPrevious() and getCurrent() (both OnTradeOrderInfo) — diff them to see exactly what changed (e.g. SL/TP).
  • Order operation enum differs from trading. Streaming uses SUB_OP_* (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE), not the OC_OP_* used by order_send — same operations, different enum.
  • Close to stop the subscription — see Streams.
  • No events without activity. If nothing trades, nothing fires.

docs.title: 1) Log new orders
docs.text:
static String label(SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE t) {
    return switch (t) {
        case SUB_OP_BUY -> "BUY";            case SUB_OP_SELL -> "SELL";
        case SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT -> "BUY LIMIT"; case SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT -> "SELL LIMIT";
        case SUB_OP_BUYSTOP -> "BUY STOP";   case SUB_OP_SELLSTOP -> "SELL STOP";
        default -> "?";
    };
}

static Subscription logNewOrders(MT4Account account) {
    return account.onTrade(ev -> {
        for (var o : ev.getEventData().getNewOrdersList())
            System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "[NEW] %s #%d %s @ %.5f%n",
                    label(o.getType()), o.getTicket(), o.getSymbol(), o.getOpenPrice());
    }, null);
}

docs.title: 2) Watch SL/TP changes
docs.text:
Use the previous/current pair to report exactly what moved.

static Subscription watchModifications(MT4Account account) {
    return account.onTrade(ev -> {
        for (var upd : ev.getEventData().getUpdatedOrdersList()) {
            var cur = upd.getCurrent(); var prev = upd.getPrevious();
            if (cur.getStopLoss() != prev.getStopLoss() || cur.getTakeProfit() != prev.getTakeProfit())
                System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, "[MOD] #%d %s SL %.5f->%.5f TP %.5f->%.5f%n",
                        cur.getTicket(), cur.getSymbol(), prev.getStopLoss(), cur.getStopLoss(),
                        prev.getTakeProfit(), cur.getTakeProfit());
        }
    }, null);
}

docs.title: 3) Fire a callback on any close
docs.text:
static Subscription onClose(MT4Account account, Consumer<OnTradeOrderInfo> callback) {
    return account.onTrade(ev ->
            ev.getEventData().getRemovedOrdersList().forEach(callback), null);
}

// usage:
// var sub = onClose(account, o -> System.out.printf("[CLOSE] #%d %s%n", o.getTicket(), o.getSymbol()));

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong enum. Order operations here are SUB_OP_*, not OC_OP_* — mixing them silently mismatches.
  • No close = leak. Always stop the stream by closing the Subscription.
  • Quiet periods. No trading activity → no events.
  • Updates need before/after. Compare getPrevious() vs getCurrent() rather than assuming what changed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Market open. Open then close a 0.01 order while subscribed — you see it in newOrders then removedOrders.
  • Modification. Change an order's SL and assert it appears in updatedOrders with differing previous/current.
  • Clean stop. Closing the Subscription ends delivery without leaking threads.

docs.title: MT4Service — Overview
docs.text:
The mid-level facade: the same operations as MT4Account, but with friendlier Java signatures.

MT4Service is Layer 2. It wraps a connected MT4Account and:

  • accepts string enums (timeframe = "H1", sort = "open_desc") instead of protobuf constants,
  • takes friendly arguments (side/type, lots, sl, tp, magic, deviationPips) and maps them to the raw request,
  • adds trade shortcuts (buyMarket, sellLimit, close, …) that return the ticket directly,
  • fills sensible defaults (e.g. a history window for quoteHistory from timeframe × limit).

Unlike the Python original, it returns the typed protobuf …Data messages (not flattened lists) — list filtering/formatting and risk math live one layer up in MT4Sugar.

Defined in MT4Service.java.

MT4Sugar    (HIGH)   one-liners, risk sizing, watchers
MT4Service  (MID)    friendly facade  ← you are here
MT4Account  (LOW)    raw gRPC / protobuf

docs.title: 🚦 Method groups
docs.text:
Each group is documented on a single page.

  • 1. Account Information — accountSummary, tradeStats, tradeUnrealizedPl, equityHistory, tradeStatsEquityHistory
  • 2. Orders & History — openedOrders, openedOrdersTickets, ordersHistory
  • 3. Symbols & Quotes — symbols, quote, quoteMany, quoteHistory, symbolParamsMany, tickValueWithSize, symbolSelect, serverTimezone
  • 4. Trading Operations — orderSend, orderModify, orderCloseDelete, orderCloseBy + the trade shortcuts (buyMarket, sellMarket, buyLimit/buyStop, sellLimit/sellStop, modifySlTp, close, closePartial, closeBy, setTradeDefaults)
  • 5. Streaming Methods — onSymbolTick, onTrade, onOpenedOrdersTickets, onOpenedOrdersProfit, onConnectState

docs.title: 🔌 Construction, connection & lifecycle
docs.text:
MT4Service wraps an MT4Account you pass to its constructor.

Method Description new MT4Service(MT4Account account) Wrap a (connected or not-yet-connected) account. connectByServerName(serverName) / (serverName, timeoutSeconds) Connect via broker server name. connectByHostPort(host, port) / (host, port, timeoutSeconds) Connect to a terminal host/port. reconnect() Re-establish the session. disconnect(boolean delete) Release the session (delete the terminal instance when true). getAccount() The wrapped MT4Account. 
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Account;
import pro.mrpc.mt4.MT4Service;

try (MT4Account account = new MT4Account(12345678L, "password", null, null, "TRIAL")) {
    MT4Service service = new MT4Service(account);
    service.connectByServerName("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30);

    var s = service.accountSummary();
    System.out.println(s.getAccountBalance() + " " + s.getAccountEquity());

    service.disconnect(false);
}

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Order Entry
docs.text:
One-call market and pending entries with pip-based or absolute SL/TP, automatic normalization and defaults.

All entries ultimately build an OrderSendRequest and call MT4Service.orderSend; they return the new ticket (long). SL/TP can be given as pip distances (slPips/tpPips) or absolute prices (slPrice/tpPrice). Lots are normalized to the volume step; a null magic/deviationPips falls back to the defaults from setDefaults. Rejections throw OrderRejected.

docs.title: placeOrder(...)
docs.text:
public long placeOrder(String side, String orderType, String symbol, Double price, Double lots,
                       Double slPips, Double tpPips, Double slPrice, Double tpPrice,
                       String comment, Integer magic, Double deviationPips)

The generic entry the shortcuts delegate to. side = "buy"/"sell", orderType = "market"/"limit"/"stop". symbol may be null to use the default symbol; price is required for limit/stop; lots defaults to 0.01 when null. For market orders the entry price is read live (ask for buy, bid for sell), and pip-based SL/TP are computed from it.

long t = sugar.placeOrder("buy", "market", "EURUSD", null, 0.01, 50.0, 100.0, null, null, "entry", null, null);

docs.title: 🧩 Notes
docs.text:
• Pips vs absolute. Pass slPips/tpPips for distances from the entry, or slPrice/tpPrice for exact prices — if both are given, the absolute price wins.
  • Sides. For a BUY, SL is below entry and TP above; for a SELL it's mirrored — Sugar works this out from side.
  • Rate-limited. Order sends pass through an internal rate limiter to avoid flooding the gateway.
  • Hook. A successful send emits on_order_sent ({ticket, symbol}) on sugar.hooks.

docs.text:

Set SL/TP at absolute prices (normalized to the symbol grid). null leaves a side unchanged.

MT4Sugar.Quote q = sugar.lastQuote("EURUSD");
sugar.modifySlTpByPrice(ticket, q.bid - sugar.pipsToPrice("EURUSD", 60), q.ask + sugar.pipsToPrice("EURUSD", 140));

docs.text:
public void close(int ticket)
public void closePartial(int ticket, double lots)

close fully closes a market order (or deletes a pending); closePartial closes part of the volume, leaving the remainder open (lots <= 0 is a no-op).

sugar.closePartial(ticket, 0.01);
sugar.close(ticket);

docs.text:
public void closeBy(int ticketA, int ticketB)
public void closeByTickets(int ticketA, int ticketB)
